This command replays them, skipping records already written, and moves each processed manifest to ~/.ubunye/fallback/synced/. How it works: Interfaces.

ubunye sync lineage                    # replay all run record manifests
ubunye sync lineage --run-id abc123    # replay one run
ubunye sync lineage --lineage-backend delta --lineage-dir main.ops.ubunye_runs
ubunye sync registry                   # replay all registry manifests
ubunye sync registry --run-id abc123
Flag Applies to Default Description --run-id both Replay only this run's manifest --lineage-backend sync lineage $UBUNYE_LINEAGE_BACKEND, else filesystem The run record store to replay into --lineage-dir sync lineage .ubunye/lineage The store's location, as given

docs.title: ubunye deploy
docs.text:
Deploy or run a task on a remote platform. Each platform has a guide under Deployment. These commands take --task/-t (repeat it to run several tasks in order, except on Databricks) and -m defaults to PROD.

A problem you can fix (no targets.yaml, no token, a cloud CLI not on PATH, a config that does not validate) ends in one [ERROR] message that says what, where and what to try, with exit code 1. ubunye export works the same way.

docs.title: deploy databricks
docs.text:
Deploy a task to Databricks as a scheduled job.

ubunye deploy databricks -d pipelines -u fraud_detection -p ingestion -t claim_etl --target nonprod
ubunye deploy databricks -d pipelines -u fraud_detection -p ingestion -t claim_etl --target nonprod --dry-run

Common flags: -d -u -p and -t (one task), all required; -m (default PROD); -dt. Plus:

Flag Default Description --target dev Deploy target from targets.yaml --dry-run false Print the job spec without deploying --host $DATABRICKS_HOST Databricks host, used only when there is no targets.yaml --token DATABRICKS_TOKEN Name of the env var that holds the token --run false Start a run of the job after deploying it, and print its link

targets.yaml is read from <usecase-dir>/<usecase>/targets.yaml, and a targets.yaml in the task folder overrides it. See Databricks authentication.

docs.title: deploy glue
docs.text:
Run a task on AWS Glue 5 (Spark 3.5), with the aws CLI. See One command to the cloud.

ubunye deploy glue -d pipelines -u shop -p orders -t clean \
    --bucket my-bucket --role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/glue-job --dry-run

Common flags -d -u -p -t (required), plus the shared launch flags and:

Flag Required Default Description --bucket yes S3 bucket for the task, script and wheel --role yes IAM role ARN the Glue job runs as --region no AWS region --job no from the task Glue job name --engine no ubunye-engine pip requirement for the engine --engine-wheel no Install this wheel instead --workers no 2 Number of workers --worker-type no G.1X Glue worker type

docs.title: deploy dataproc
docs.text:
Run a task on GCP Dataproc Serverless, in a container image, with gcloud. See One command to the cloud.

Common flags -d -u -p -t (required), plus the shared launch flags and:

Flag Required Default Description --project yes GCP project --region yes GCP region --bucket yes GCS bucket for the task and script --image yes Container image with the engine (see deploy dockerfile dataproc) --service-account no Service account the batch runs as --runtime no 2.2 Dataproc Serverless runtime version --batch no from the task Batch id

docs.title: deploy k8s
docs.text:
Run a task as a Kubernetes Job, with kubectl (its current context). The image comes from deploy dockerfile container, with the pipelines baked in, so there is no -d. See One command to the cloud.

Common flags -u -p -t (required), plus the shared launch flags and:

Flag Short Required Default Description --image yes Image from deploy dockerfile container --namespace -n no default Kubernetes namespace --job no from the task Job name --cpu no 1 CPU request --memory no 2Gi Memory request --timeout no 1800 Seconds to wait for the job

docs.title: deploy container-apps
docs.text:
Run a task as an Azure Container Apps job, with the az CLI. Like k8s, the image holds the pipelines. See One command to the cloud.

Common flags -u -p -t (required), plus the shared launch flags and:

Flag Short Required Default Description --image yes Image from deploy dockerfile container --resource-group -g yes Azure resource group --environment yes Container Apps environment --job no from the task Job name --registry-server no Registry server --registry-identity no Managed identity (resource id) that pulls the image --cpu no 2 CPU --memory no 4Gi Memory --timeout no 1800 Seconds a replica may run

docs.title: deploy emr-serverless
docs.text:
Start a task run on AWS EMR Serverless, with the aws CLI. It does not wait for the run to finish, so it has no --wait or --record-out. See One command to the cloud.

Common flags -u -p -t (required), -m (default PROD), -dt, --var. Plus:

Flag Required Default Description --application-id yes An application whose image is from deploy dockerfile emr-serverless --role yes Job execution role ARN --bucket yes S3 bucket for the job's logs --region no AWS region --env no Environment for the task, KEY=VALUE (repeatable) --dry-run no false Print the plan; run nothing

docs.title: Shared launch flags
docs.text:
glue, dataproc, k8s and container-apps also take:

Flag Short Default Description --mode -m PROD Profile --data-timestamp -dt Data timestamp --env Environment for the task, KEY=VALUE (repeatable) --var Template variable, KEY=VALUE (repeatable) --wait / --no-wait wait Follow the run to its end --record-out Save the run's record here (for ubunye gate); with several tasks, one file each: NAME.TASK.json --dry-run false Print the plan; run nothing

docs.title: deploy dockerfile
docs.text:
Write a Dockerfile for a Spark job image on PLATFORM (dataproc, emr-serverless or container), and the entry script next to it.

ubunye deploy dockerfile container --pipelines pipelines --out build/Dockerfile
Flag Default Description --pipelines pipelines Folder copied into the image as /app/pipelines --engine ubunye-engine pip requirement for the engine --out Write here instead of printing. A folder, or a path ending in / such as img/, gets <folder>/Dockerfile; missing folders are made

docs.title: ubunye export
docs.text:
Generate orchestration artifacts from a task's config.yaml. Defaults come from the config's ORCHESTRATION block (see Orchestration).

ubunye export defaults to production (--profile prod for airflow and databricks, -m PROD for spark-pipeline), while ubunye run defaults to DEV: an export is what a scheduler runs, a run is usually a try on your own machine. Pass the profile you mean when it matters.

docs.title: export airflow
docs.text:
Generate an Airflow DAG (Airflow 2.4+ and 3) that runs the task with the CLI.

ubunye export airflow \
    -c pipelines/fraud_detection/ingestion/claim_etl/config.yaml \
    -o dags/claim_etl.py
Flag Short Required Default Description --config -c yes Path to the task's config.yaml --output -o yes Where to write the DAG --profile no prod Profile put in the bash command as -m. Lower case by default, while ubunye run defaults to DEV: pass --profile PROD if your profiles are upper case --usecase-dir no this folder The pipelines folder where Airflow runs --backend no Backend for the run --lineage no false Write a run record for each run

docs.title: export databricks
docs.text:
Generate a Databricks Jobs API spec (job.json) for the task.

ubunye export databricks \
    -c pipelines/fraud_detection/ingestion/claim_etl/config.yaml \
    -o jobs/claim_etl.json
Flag Short Required Default Description --config -c yes Path to the task's config.yaml --output -o yes Where to write job.json --profile no prod Profile put in the job command as -m. Lower case by default, as for export airflow

docs.title: export spark-pipeline
docs.text:
Write the task as a Spark Declarative Pipeline (Spark 4.1+), to run with spark-pipelines.

ubunye export spark-pipeline \
    -c pipelines/fraud_detection/ingestion/claim_etl/config.yaml \
    -o sdp/claim_etl

Common flags: -m (default PROD), -dt, --var. Plus:

Flag Short Required Default Description --config -c yes Path to the task's config.yaml --output -o yes Folder to write the pipeline into --storage no a folder inside the output Pipeline storage URI --name no Pipeline name --catalog no Catalog --database no Database

docs.title: ubunye models
docs.text:
Manage ML model versions and their lifecycle.

Every subcommand takes:

Flag Short Required Description --use-case -u yes Use case grouping (note the hyphen: other commands say --usecase) --model -m yes Model name (here -m is not the profile) --store -s yes Model store path --backend -b no Registry backend: an entry point in ubunye.registry_backends (filesystem, mlflow, a plugin). Default UBUNYE_REGISTRY_BACKEND, else filesystem. See Interfaces

info, promote, demote, rollback and archive also require --version (-v). list and compare take --json.

docs.title: models list
docs.text: ubunye models list -u fraud_detection -m FraudRiskModel -s .ubunye/model_store

docs.title: models info
docs.text: ubunye models info -u fraud_detection -m FraudRiskModel -v 1.3.0 -s .ubunye/model_store

docs.title: models promote
docs.text:
ubunye models promote -u fraud_detection -m FraudRiskModel -v 1.3.0 \
    --to production --promoted-by alice -s .ubunye/model_store

Target stages: staging, production.

The version must pass the model's promotion gates first: the promotion_gates its training run registered it with (for example min_auc: 0.85). If one fails, nothing is promoted and the failing gate is named. --force promotes anyway, prints which gates were skipped, and marks the version (promotion_forced) so the skip stays on the record. See Model registry.

docs.title: models demote
docs.text:
ubunye models demote -u fraud_detection -m FraudRiskModel -v 1.3.0 \
    --to staging -s .ubunye/model_store

Target stages: development, staging, archived.

Demote only moves a version down. staging is allowed only from production; production is never a choice. To move a version up, use models promote, which checks the promotion gates.

docs.title: models rollback
docs.text:
ubunye models rollback -u fraud_detection -m FraudRiskModel -v 1.2.0 -s .ubunye/model_store

Archives the current production version and restores --version to production.

docs.title: models archive
docs.text: ubunye models archive -u fraud_detection -m FraudRiskModel -v 1.1.0 -s .ubunye/model_store

docs.title: models compare
docs.text:
ubunye models compare -u fraud_detection -m FraudRiskModel \
    --versions 1.2.0 --versions 1.3.0 -s .ubunye/model_store

docs.title: ubunye prove
docs.text:
The proving ground: run one workload on many environments, turn each run record into an observation, and compare them. See Proving ground.

ubunye prove observe --workload c01 --env pandas-local -d . -u uc -p pkg -t task -o evidence
ubunye prove observe --workload c01 --env aws-glue --record glue.json -o evidence
ubunye prove skip    --workload c01 --env azure --status not_run --reason "..." -o evidence
ubunye prove report  evidence --workload c01 --reference spark-local --expect aws-glue

docs.title: prove observe
docs.text:
Turn a run record into an observation of a workload in an environment. Name the record with --record FILE, or with -d -u -p -t and --run-id (default latest). Several tasks (-t a -t b) give one observation each, named <workload>-<task>.

Flag Short Required Default Description --workload yes The workload's id, e.g. c01-portable-etl --env yes The environment's name, e.g. spark-local --out -o no evidence The evidence folder --record no A run record JSON file -d -u -p -t no Find the record in the run record store --run-id no latest A stored run's id, or latest --kind no local local, cloud or managed --provider no aws, gcp, azure, databricks, ... --runtime no e.g. Glue 5.0, Dataproc Serverless 2.2 --region no Region --cost-amount no Cost of the run --cost-currency no USD Currency --cost-basis no local for --kind local, else unknown actual, provider_estimate, ubunye_estimate, local or unknown --cost-source no How the figure was obtained --run-url no Where a reader can check this run

docs.title: prove skip
docs.text:
Record that an environment did not run the workload, and why. Takes --workload, --env and --reason (all required), --status (not_run (default), unsupported or failed_to_launch), -o/--out (default evidence) and --run-url.

--kind, --cost-basis and --status take only the values listed. Any other value is a usage error (exit 2) that lists the choices.

docs.title: prove report
docs.text: Compare every observation of a workload in the EVIDENCE folder with the --reference environment, and exit 1 if any run disagrees. --expect takes a comma-separated list of environments; one with no evidence is reported as NOT RUN. --json FILE and --md FILE write the matrix and the table.

docs.title: ubunye mcp
docs.text:
Serve the engine to agents over MCP (stdio). Its tools: tasks, doctor, plan, runs, health, upstream, gate, focus, and run when allowed. See Agents over MCP.

ubunye mcp -d pipelines
ubunye mcp -d pipelines --allow-run
Flag Short Default Description --usecase-dir -d . The pipelines folder the server works in --allow-run false Offer the run tool (every other tool only reads) --allow-live-llm false Let run call models live (default: replay, no key, no spend) --lineage-dir .ubunye/lineage As for lineage --lineage-backend $UBUNYE_LINEAGE_BACKEND, else filesystem As for lineage

docs.title: ubunye plugins
docs.text:
List the readers, writers and transforms discovered through entry points. See Writing a plugin.

ubunye plugins

docs.title: ubunye version
docs.text:
ubunye version
# Ubunye Engine v0.9.1

The version comes from the installed package metadata.

python -m ubunye is a different, smaller runner

python -m ubunye is not this CLI. It is a small runner for spark-submit on platforms with no console script (EMR Serverless, Dataproc Serverless, YARN, Kubernetes): it runs one task, python -m ubunye --task-dir <folder with config.yaml> --mode PROD --dt <dt>, attached to the SparkSession spark-submit made. Its only other flags are --lineage and --log-level. --task-dir must be a local folder; a bucket URI (s3://, gs://) does not work. To run from a bucket, use ubunye deploy glue, dataproc or emr-serverless. See Deploy anywhere.

docs.title: Contributing to Ubunye Engine
docs.text: Thank you for helping. Ubunye is built in the open, from Africa, for anyone who runs data and ML pipelines. This page is everything you need to make a change that gets merged.

docs.title: Ways to help
docs.text:
• Report a bug: what you ran, what you expected, what happened (the full error), and your Python, OS, and Spark or pandas versions.
  • Ask for a feature: the problem first, then the config or API you would like, and what it would cost.
  • Fix something: bugs, docs, tests, examples.
  • Add a plugin: a reader, writer, transform, hook or a whole backend, from your own package, with no change to the engine. See Execution Backends and the plugin guide.

Issues and pull requests: https://github.com/ubunye-ai-ecosystems/ubunye_engine.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ubunye-ai-ecosystems/ubunye_engine.git
cd ubunye_engine
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate            # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -U pip
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pre-commit install

[dev] includes pandas and pyarrow, so the whole unit tier runs with no Java.

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
Tier Command Needs Unit pytest tests/unit -m "not integration" nothing else Spark pytest tests/integration Java (supported versions) and pip install -e ".[spark,delta]" Types python -m mypy ubunye nothing else Lint pre-commit run --all-files nothing else Docs pip install -r docs/requirements.txt && mkdocs build --strict nothing else Performance python benchmarks/guard.py --base <checkout of the base branch> a second checkout (git worktree add ../base origin/main)

The Spark tier includes the parity suite, which runs the same data through Spark and pandas and checks they agree on types, values, files and run records. Any change to how data is read, written or hashed must keep it green. It also runs the backend conformance suite (ubunye.testing.backend_conformance, which a new backend runs too) and a distributed check: one task on a single core and on a two-executor Spark must leave the same run record, with the driver's result size capped far below the data, so nothing may pull rows back to the driver.

How to write a unit test (with no Spark) or a Spark test: see Writing tests in the Developer Guide.

CI also times every pull request against the branch it goes into (benchmarks/guard.py) and fails it if an operation gets more than 30% slower.

docs.title: How a change is made
docs.text:
1. Write the failing test first. It should fail for the reason you are fixing, then pass with the fix. A change without a test is not finished.
  2. One commit per fix or feature, with a message that says what was wrong and why this is the right fix, in the Conventional Commits style (fix(pandas): ..., feat(cli): ..., docs: ...).
  3. Docs and changelog in the same commit. If users would notice the change, update the page they would read and add a line under ## [Unreleased] in docs/changelog.md.
  4. Never skip the hooks (--no-verify). If a hook fails, fix the cause.
  5. Nothing that works today breaks. Configs, CLI flags, Python calls and notebooks keep working; anything renamed keeps its old name with a deprecation warning for at least one release.
  6. The core stays engine free. Code in ubunye/core never imports Spark, pandas or pyarrow (a test checks every import). Engines are adapters, found through entry points.

Then open a pull request against main and say what changed, why, and how you tested it. CI runs the unit tier on Python 3.10 to 3.13 on Linux, Windows and macOS, and again on the oldest versions of every dependency the package accepts; the Spark tier runs on Spark 3.5 and Spark 4.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text: Plain language, short sentences. Explain a term the first time. Say what the code does and why, not how clever it is. Error messages say what went wrong, where, and what to try.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: Maintainers release by bumping the version on main; the publish to PyPI waits for a person to approve it.

docs.title: Databricks Authentication
docs.text: This page shows how CI signs in to a Databricks workspace. It is for whoever wires a GitHub repository to a workspace.

docs.title: Which auth does which command use?
docs.text:
Command Personal access token Service principal (OAuth M2M) ubunye deploy databricks (and the workflow ubunye init github-actions writes) Yes, the only option No databricks bundle deploy / bundle run (Databricks Asset Bundles) Yes Yes, recommended on paid workspaces

ubunye deploy databricks reads a token from DATABRICKS_TOKEN, or from the variable named by --token or by token_env in targets.yaml. If that variable is empty it stops with AuthNotFoundError; a token the workspace rejects gives AuthInvalidError. See Errors. It never uses the service principal secrets below. The two ways to deploy are compared on the Databricks deploy page.

docs.title: The words
docs.text:
• Personal access token (PAT): a long secret string, like a password, that acts as one user. Anyone holding it can do what that user can do.
  • Service principal: a robot user that belongs to the workspace, not to a person. You give it only the rights CI needs.
  • OAuth M2M (machine to machine): how a service principal signs in. It uses a client ID and a client secret instead of a token.

docs.title: Which repository gets the secrets?
docs.text:
Set the secrets on the GitHub repository whose workflow runs the deploy:

  • Your own pipelines repo, for your own jobs.
  • This engine repo (ubunye-ai-ecosystems/ubunye_engine), for its bundle workflows .github/workflows/*_databricks*.yml, which deploy examples/production/*_databricks.
  • The examples repo (ubunye-examples), for its deploy workflow.

The steps are the same in each.

docs.title: The two flows
docs.text:
Pick one per workspace.

Flow When to use Secrets Personal access token Free Edition, a workspace with one user, quick experiments, and always for ubunye deploy databricks DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_TOKEN Service principal with OAuth (recommended for paid workspaces) Production, shared workspaces, audit trails, secrets you rotate in the UI DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID, DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET

The Databricks CLI picks the flow for you: if DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID and DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET are both set, it uses OAuth M2M. Otherwise it uses the token. You choose a flow by which secrets you set, not in the workflow.

docs.title: Option A: Personal Access Token (Free Edition)
docs.text:
Free Edition has no service principals, so PAT is the only option there.

  1. In the workspace UI: User Settings → Developer → Access tokens → Generate new token.
  2. In the GitHub repo: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret:
    • DATABRICKS_HOST: e.g. https://dbc-xxxxxxxx-xxxx.cloud.databricks.com
    • DATABRICKS_TOKEN: the token from step 1.
  3. Leave DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID / DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET unset.

docs.title: Option B: Service Principal + OAuth (recommended)
docs.text: On paid workspaces, use a service principal so deploys are not tied to a human user's PAT. The principal is a durable workspace identity that can be granted only the permissions the CI needs.

docs.title: 1. Create a service principal
docs.text:
Account console (https://accounts.cloud.databricks.com) → User management → Service principals → Add service principal.

Note the Application ID that appears after creation: that is your DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID. It is a UUID, not a name.

docs.title: 2. Add the principal to the workspace
docs.text: Account console → Workspaces → your workspace → Permissions → Add. Grant the principal User access. (Admin access is not required for bundle deploy; see step 4 for the grants you actually need.)

docs.title: 3. Generate an OAuth secret
docs.text:
Workspace UI → Settings → Identity and access → Service principals → your principal → Secrets → Generate secret.

Copy the secret once: it is not shown again. That is your DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET.

docs.title: 4. Grant the principal workspace access
docs.text:
The principal needs to be able to:

  • Write to the workspace files root used by DABs (/Workspace/Users/<principal>/.bundle/...).
  • Deploy and run jobs.
  • Write to the Unity Catalog schema and volumes the examples create.

On paid workspaces with Unity Catalog, the minimum grants are:

-- Replace <sp_id> with the service principal's Application ID.
GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG main TO `<sp_id>`;
GRANT CREATE SCHEMA ON CATALOG main TO `<sp_id>`;
GRANT USE SCHEMA, CREATE TABLE, CREATE VOLUME ON SCHEMA main.ubunye_examples TO `<sp_id>`;

(Replace main / ubunye_examples with the catalog and schema you deploy against. The examples repo defaults to workspace / ubunye_examples.)

CREATE VOLUME is not optional if you train models: the model registry is a directory of files, and a Unity Catalog volume is the only writable path on serverless compute, and the executors cannot see the driver's /tmp.

docs.title: 5. Add the three secrets to GitHub
docs.text:
Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret:

Secret Value DATABRICKS_HOST e.g. https://adb-1234567890.12.azuredatabricks.net DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID The service principal's Application ID (UUID). DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET The OAuth secret from step 3.

Do not also set DATABRICKS_TOKEN. If both are present, the CLI picks OAuth, but leaving a stale PAT around defeats the point of moving off it.

ubunye deploy databricks cannot use these three secrets: it needs a token (see the table at the top).

docs.title: How the workflows consume these secrets
docs.text:
Every Databricks bundle workflow in this engine repo (.github/workflows/*_databricks*.yml) and the examples repo's deploy workflow export the same env block:

env:
  DATABRICKS_HOST:          ${{ secrets.DATABRICKS_HOST }}
  DATABRICKS_TOKEN:         ${{ secrets.DATABRICKS_TOKEN }}
  DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID:     ${{ secrets.DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID }}
  DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET }}

The Check for Databricks secrets step gates the deploy on either flow being wired up:

if [[ -z "${DATABRICKS_HOST}" ]]; then
  has_secrets=false
elif [[ -n "${DATABRICKS_TOKEN}" ]] || \
     [[ -n "${DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID}" && -n "${DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET}" ]]; then
  has_secrets=true
else
  has_secrets=false
fi

If the gate is false, the workflow runs the unit tests and portability diff but skips bundle validate / deploy / run. This keeps PRs from forks green.

docs.title: Verifying the wiring
docs.text:
These steps use the examples repo; the same checks work for any repo.

  1. Push a trivial change to the examples repo (e.g. edit its README) and merge it.
  2. Watch the deploy workflow in the ubunye-examples repository. The databricks bundle deploy step logs a line like Uploading bundle files to /Workspace/Users/<principal>/.bundle/.... If <principal> is the service principal's Application ID, OAuth is active. If it's a human email address, the CLI fell back to PAT.
  3. In the workspace UI: Workflows → the deployed job → Run as should show the service principal, not a human user.

docs.title: Rotating the OAuth secret
docs.text:
OAuth secrets expire (default 1 year). To rotate:

  1. Generate a new secret for the same principal (step 3 above).
  2. Update DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET in GitHub.
  3. Delete the old secret in the workspace UI.

The DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID does not change: it is the principal's identity.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Error: default auth: cannot configure default credentials None of the three secrets are set, or DATABRICKS_HOST is blank. Confirm all three are populated under Settings → Secrets. 401 Unauthorized on bundle deploy Secret is correct but the principal lacks workspace access. Re-check step 2 / step 4. PERMISSION_DENIED: User is not allowed to write to path /Workspace/... Principal has workspace access but not write access to the bundle root. Grant WRITE on /Workspace/Users/<sp_id>/ or let the CLI pick a different root via bundle deploy --var="root_path=...". SCHEMA_NOT_FOUND when the job runs Principal can deploy but not create the UC schema. Add CREATE SCHEMA ON CATALOG <cat> grant. Deploy succeeds on Free Edition but OAuth fails Free Edition does not support service principals. Use PAT (Option A).

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
This page is the map for running your tasks somewhere other than your laptop. It says where you can deploy today, which page has the steps, and the one rule every target shares. It is for anyone moving a task off a laptop.

Deployment means one thing here: something launches your task, in an environment, with credentials, often on a schedule. The task folder itself never changes.

docs.title: Which page do I need?
docs.text: You want to... Read run a task as a Databricks job Databricks sign in to Databricks from CI (token or service principal) Databricks authentication run a task on AWS Glue, GCP Dataproc, Kubernetes, Azure or EMR with one command One command to the cloud run a task on Azure Container Apps Azure use the companion repo's scripts for AWS or GCP AWS, GCP run on your own Kubernetes cluster Kubernetes launch with spark-submit on any Spark cluster Anywhere with spark-submit check the same task gives the same data everywhere Proving ground: latest results

docs.title: Where you can deploy today
docs.text:
This table is the one place that says what is proven. "Proven" means the proving ground ran real workloads there and got the same data as local Spark.

Environment Command Status Page Databricks ubunye deploy databricks, or Databricks Asset Bundles Proven, and runs in CI Databricks AWS Glue 5 ubunye deploy glue Proven One command to the cloud GCP Dataproc Serverless ubunye deploy dataproc Proven One command to the cloud Azure Container Apps ubunye deploy container-apps Proven Azure Kubernetes ubunye deploy k8s Proven on a local kind cluster Kubernetes Docker images ubunye deploy dockerfile Working; the base for Kubernetes, Azure, Dataproc and EMR One command to the cloud AWS EMR Serverless ubunye deploy emr-serverless Planned: tested as a plan only. A free plan AWS account cannot use EMR One command to the cloud AWS EMR Serverless, GCP Dataproc (companion repo scripts) platforms/aws/submit.sh, platforms/gcp/submit.sh Written, not yet run AWS, GCP Classic EMR on EC2 (YARN) SPARK_MASTER=yarn in the companion repo's launcher Not yet run AWS Any Spark cluster with spark-submit python -m ubunye Supported Anywhere SageMaker, Vertex AI (serving a promoted model) none yet Planned; these serve models, they do not run pipelines AWS, GCP

docs.title: The spark.master rule
docs.text:
One rule applies everywhere: the task never chooses its own cluster. Leave spark.master out of your config.yaml.

spark.master is the Spark setting that says where the work runs: one machine (local[*]), YARN, Kubernetes, and so on. Whoever launches the job owns that choice:

  • Databricks, Glue, EMR Serverless and Dataproc set it themselves.
  • On a laptop, the launcher sets it (the companion repo's platforms/local/run.sh sets local[*]).
  • With spark-submit, the --master flag sets it.

If your config sets spark.master and the platform already chose a different one, the engine stops with a SparkSessionError that names both values. It does this on purpose. Under spark-submit, a config that wins this fight makes the whole job run inside the driver: it ignores every worker, reports success, and bills you for a cluster it never used. An error is better than that.

The same goes for other settings fixed when Spark starts, such as spark.sql.extensions: see Engine settings.

docs.title: Two ways to build an image
docs.text:
Kubernetes, Azure, Dataproc and EMR run your task from a container image. Each deploy page says which of these two it uses:

Way Command Used by The engine writes the Dockerfile ubunye deploy dockerfile container, ... dataproc, ... emr-serverless ubunye deploy k8s, container-apps, dataproc, emr-serverless The companion repo's Dockerfiles docker build -f platforms/docker/Dockerfile . (and Dockerfile.ml for models) the ubunye-examples scripts and manifests

docs.title: Moved from this page
docs.text: The Databricks Asset Bundles flow, the GitHub Actions workflow, the Python API on Databricks and the dev notebooks now live on the Databricks page.

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text: How the engine is built inside, and where to change it. For contributors and for anyone extending Ubunye beyond what config can do. To set up, run the tests and get a change merged, read Contributing.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
Entry points:
    CLI (ubunye run)  --+
    Python API        --+
                        |
                        v
                    load_config()         YAML + Jinja2, then Pydantic v2
                        |
                        v
                    task_runner.execute_user_task()
                        |
                        v
                    Engine.run(cfg)
                        +-- Backend.start()   spark, databricks, pandas or a plugin
                        +-- registry.readers[format]().read()     [per input]
                        +-- Transform.apply()                     [the user's Task]
                        +-- registry.writers[format]().write()    [per output]
                        +-- Backend.stop()
                        |
                        v
                    LineageRecorder (if --lineage), as a hook

docs.title: Engine library layout
docs.text:
The ubunye/ package, folder by folder. For the layout of your project (use cases, pipelines, tasks), see Project Structure.

ubunye/
├── api.py          : public Python API (run_task, run_pipeline)
├── notebook.py     : ubunye.notebook(), step by step runs in a notebook
├── mcp_server.py   : `ubunye mcp`, the engine as an MCP server for agents
├── core/           : runtime (Engine), task runner, interfaces (Reader, Writer,
│                     Transform, Task, Backend), ports, capabilities, expectations,
│                     planning, write modes, run leases (runs.py), gate, errors.
│                     Never imports Spark, pandas or pyarrow.
├── config/         : YAML loader, Jinja resolver, Pydantic schema, variables, config hash
├── backends/
│   ├── spark_backend.py      : creates a new SparkSession
│   ├── databricks_backend.py : reuses the active SparkSession (Databricks)
│   └── pandas_backend.py     : pandas and pyarrow, no Java
├── adapters/       : engine specific mechanics behind the core's contracts
│   ├── spark/      : session setup, writes and claimed appends, Delta and JDBC
│   │                 batches, Delta read pinning, content hash, held outputs
│   └── pandas_*.py : pandas reads and writes, partition folders, run record facts;
│                     plus CSV and JSON parsing that matches Spark's
├── plugins/
│   ├── readers/    : hive, jdbc, unity, rest_api, s3, delta, binary
│   ├── writers/    : s3, jdbc, unity, rest_api, delta, hive (no binary writer)
│   ├── transforms/ : noop, model_transform
│   ├── ml/         : BaseModel, SklearnModel, SparkMLModel (internal wrappers)
│   ├── llm.py      : language model backends (anthropic, openai_compatible,
│   │                 databricks_serving)
│   └── secrets.py  : secret:// stores (env, file, databricks, aws-sm, gcp-sm, azure-kv)
├── llm/            : the language model port a task calls: budget, cost estimate,
│                     prices, progress, replay
├── models/         : UbunyeModel contract, loader, registry and its backends
│                     (filesystem, MLflow), gates, lifecycle, artifact stores
├── interfaces/     : typing.Protocol contracts for the pluggable seams: deploy,
│                     registry, run record stores, auth
├── lineage/        : run records: context, recorder, row hashing, code and machine
│                     evidence, source versions, stores (filesystem, Delta), health
│                     and upstream queries, OpenLineage, FOCUS
├── proving/        : the proving ground: observations, the comparison matrix
├── cli/            : main plus one module per command group (lineage, models,
│                     deploy, prove, gate, runs, sync, export, init, ...)
├── deploy/         : Databricks (bundle, workspace, auth), Glue and Dataproc
│                     (cloud.py), Kubernetes, Container Apps and EMR Serverless
│                     (containers.py), the task zip (package.py)
├── orchestration/  : Airflow, Databricks job and Spark pipeline exporters
├── telemetry/      : events, MLflow, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, hooks/
├── testing/        : conformance suites for people who extend Ubunye (backend,
│                     run record store, registry)
└── _internal/      : not public: entry point discovery, auto detection,
                      metadata helper

The package ships its type information (ubunye/py.typed), so your type checker sees Ubunye's types. mypy checks the engine on every pull request (the "Types (mypy)" CI job).

docs.title: Config loading pipeline
docs.text:
1. Read raw YAML: load_config(path, variables) in ubunye/config/loader.py.
  2. Jinja2 render: resolve_config(raw, cli_vars=...) renders every string value. Variables come from -dt, -dtf, -m (as dt, dtf, mode), --var flags, os.environ (as env.*), and task_dir (the task's own folder).
  3. Pydantic validation: the rendered YAML is parsed into UbunyeConfig. Validation is strict; an unknown field raises ConfigFieldError with a suggestion.
  4. Profile merge: UbunyeConfig.merged_spark_conf(mode) merges base and profile Spark conf. A mode that names no profile raises ConfigProfileError when the config has profiles.

Key files:

  • ubunye/config/loader.py: load_config
  • ubunye/config/resolver.py: the Jinja resolver
  • ubunye/config/schema.py: all Pydantic models

docs.title: Plugin registry
docs.text:
ubunye.core.runtime.Registry.from_entrypoints() discovers readers, writers and transforms via importlib.metadata.entry_points. Other groups are loaded where they are used (most through ubunye/_internal/discovery.py). Every group below is registered in pyproject.toml; the shipped plugins use the same groups a third party would. How to write one: Writing a plugin.

# Entry point groups
ubunye.readers            Reader subclasses
ubunye.writers            Writer subclasses
ubunye.transforms         Transform subclasses
ubunye.backends           Backend subclasses (see Execution backends)
ubunye.hooks              Hook classes (loaded when UBUNYE_TELEMETRY is set)
ubunye.monitors           Monitor implementations (CONFIG.monitors)
ubunye.ml                 ML model adapters
ubunye.secrets            secret:// stores
ubunye.llm_backends       language model backends (llm.port("anthropic", ...))
ubunye.deploy_adapters    deploy targets (databricks)
ubunye.artifact_stores    model artifact storage schemes (file)
ubunye.registry_backends  model registries (filesystem, mlflow; ADR 010)
ubunye.lineage_backends   run record stores (filesystem, delta; ADR 011)
ubunye.auth_backends      Databricks auth (token, service_principal)

registry.readers["hive"] returns the class registered as hive. The class is instantiated fresh for each read or write.

docs.title: Engine runtime
docs.text:
Engine.run(cfg) in ubunye/core/runtime.py:

  1. Check the config before anything runs: inputs and outputs, transforms exist, and the backend can do what the task needs (BackendCapabilityError if not).
  2. Build the hook chain (defaults + extra_hooks, or hooks= override).
  3. Open chain.task(ctx, cfg, state), which wraps the entire run.
  4. If manage_backend=True, start the backend.
  5. Read each input in a Reader:<format> step: Reader.read(io_cfg, backend).
  6. Apply the transform in a Transform:<type> step: Transform.apply(...).
  7. Check the output expectations (ExpectationError stops the run before any write).
  8. Write each output in a Writer:<format> step: Writer.write(...).
  9. Populate state["outputs"] so hooks can inspect them on exit.
  10. If manage_backend=True, stop the backend.

task_runner.execute_user_task puts task_dir on sys.path for the duration of the run, so transformations.py can do from model import ....

docs.title: SparkBackend
docs.text:
ubunye/backends/spark_backend.py:

  • Lazily imports pyspark: no import error if PySpark is not installed and Spark is not used.
  • Implements a context manager (with SparkBackend(app_name=..., conf={...}) as be:).
  • be.spark: the SparkSession.
  • be.conf_effective: dict of active configuration.
  • Safe for multiple start() calls (idempotent).
  • stop() stops the session only if start() created it. A session that was already running belongs to whoever started it.

docs.title: DatabricksBackend
docs.text:
ubunye/backends/databricks_backend.py:

  • Wraps an existing SparkSession instead of creating a new one.
  • If no session is passed explicitly, retrieves the active session via SparkSession.getActiveSession().
  • start() attaches to the active session (or no-ops if already attached).
  • stop() is a no-op: we do not own the session, so we never stop it.
  • Use this on Databricks where a SparkSession is always available.

docs.title: Auto-detection in the Python API
docs.text:
ubunye.run_task() and ubunye.run_pipeline() auto-detect the backend:

  1. If backend= is passed (a name such as "pandas", or a Backend instance), that backend
  2. If spark= is passed explicitly, DatabricksBackend(spark=session)
  3. If an active SparkSession exists, DatabricksBackend
  4. Otherwise the default backend (spark) with config-driven Spark conf

Passing both backend= and spark= is an error. See ADR 003.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
ubunye/api.py exposes run_task() and run_pipeline(): the same execution pipeline as the CLI but callable from Python code (notebooks, scripts, tests).

Key differences from the CLI path:

  • Backend auto-detection: picks DatabricksBackend if an active session exists, otherwise the default backend, unless backend= names one.
  • No subprocess: runs in-process, so the caller can inspect returned DataFrames directly.
  • Shared session lifecycle: when using DatabricksBackend, the session stays alive after the run.

Both functions (and notebook()) are re-exported from ubunye.__init__:

import ubunye
outputs = ubunye.run_task(task_dir="...", mode="DEV")

# Inject custom hooks (notebook/script use only)
from my_pkg.hooks import SlackAlertHook
outputs = ubunye.run_task(task_dir="...", hooks=[SlackAlertHook("#alerts")])

docs.title: Unified execution: task_runner.execute_user_task
docs.text:
api.py, cli/main.py run, and cli/test_cmd.py run all delegate to ubunye.core.task_runner.execute_user_task(). It loads the user's Task subclass from transformations.py, wraps it as an ephemeral Transform plugin (_ubunye_user_task), and runs the resulting config through Engine. One code path means hooks, lineage, and lifecycle behave identically across all three entry points.

The Engine exposes two flags that this helper relies on:

  • manage_backend=False: the caller owns backend.start() / backend.stop(), letting the CLI share one Spark session across many tasks.
  • extra_hooks=[...]: appended to the default hook set. Used to attach a MonitorHook wrapping the optional LineageRecorder without replacing the built-in telemetry hooks.

docs.title: Lineage system
docs.text:
ubunye/lineage/:

Module Responsibility context.py RunContext and StepRecord: run ID, task metadata, timestamps, facts per input and output recorder.py LineageRecorder: task_start / task_end, run as a hook through MonitorHook storage.py FileSystemLineageStore: reads and writes JSON under .ubunye/lineage/ stores.py Finds a run record store by name (ubunye.lineage_backends) and picks one: the name asked for, then UBUNYE_LINEAGE_BACKEND, then filesystem (ADR 011) delta_store.py DeltaLineageBackend: run records in a Delta table, by table name or path (ADR 011) health.py Job health as a query over run records: last result, last success, failures in a row, runs stuck in running (ADR 013) upstream.py Upstream checks (CONFIG.requires): do not start until another task succeeded for this batch (ADR 013) hasher.py Hashes of schemas and files evidence.py The code and machine hashes a run record carries content_hash.py The content hash (rows-v1): every row, any order, the same on Spark and pandas source_version.py The version of each input source when it is read and when it is hashed openlineage.py OpenLineage events from run records focus.py FOCUS cost rows for a run's model calls

The LineageRecorder is wrapped in a MonitorHook and called at task start and end. On task end it writes the run record to the chosen store; the filesystem store writes .ubunye/lineage/<usecase>/<package>/<task>/<run_id>.json (<package> is the pipeline). See ADR 006.

docs.title: Observability (hooks)
docs.text:
The Engine observes task runs through hooks: a single abstraction that wraps every task and every step in a context manager. The Engine itself does not know about Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, MLflow, or event logs.

class Hook:
    @contextmanager
    def task(self, ctx, cfg, state): yield

    @contextmanager
    def step(self, ctx, name, meta): yield

ubunye/core/hooks.py defines Hook and HookChain (multiplexer). ubunye/telemetry/hooks/ ships four hook classes, plus MonitorHook, which wraps one monitor such as the LineageRecorder. Three are telemetry hooks registered under ubunye.hooks in pyproject.toml (events, otel, prometheus). The fourth, LegacyMonitorsHook, is not registered: the engine always adds it, to run CONFIG.monitors.

File Hook Wraps hooks/events.py EventLoggerHook JSON Lines event log hooks/otel.py OTelHook OpenTelemetry spans hooks/prometheus.py PrometheusHook Prometheus counters/histograms hooks/monitors.py LegacyMonitorsHook User monitors from CONFIG.monitors (MLflow etc.)

Environment flags still apply:

  • UBUNYE_TELEMETRY=1: enable every hook registered under ubunye.hooks (the three built-in telemetry hooks, and any a third party ships)
  • UBUNYE_PROM_PORT=8000: start a Prometheus HTTP endpoint

Legacy user monitors (CONFIG.monitors) run independently of the telemetry flag, as before.

Override the hook set directly:

from ubunye.core.runtime import Engine
from my_package.hooks import SlackAlertHook

engine = Engine(hooks=[SlackAlertHook(channel="#data-alerts")])
engine.run(cfg)

See the Hooks guide for writing custom hooks.

docs.title: ML architecture
docs.text:
Two separate ML systems coexist:

System Location Purpose Internal wrappers ubunye/plugins/ml/ SklearnModel, SparkMLModel: engine-owned adapters User contract ubunye/models/ UbunyeModel ABC: user-implemented; the engine never imports ML libs

UbunyeModel (ubunye/models/base.py) is the only interface the engine calls. ModelTransform (ubunye/plugins/transforms/model_transform.py) loads the user's class dynamically via load_model_class() and calls train() or predict().

The ModelRegistry (ubunye/models/registry.py) is one API over a pluggable registry backend. Backends are found by name in ubunye.registry_backends (filesystem, the default, and mlflow), chosen by --backend / backend=, then UBUNYE_REGISTRY_BACKEND, then filesystem. The filesystem backend stores artifacts and metadata on disk, with JSON from dataclasses.asdict(). See ADR 010.

docs.title: Unit tests (Spark-free)
docs.text:
Use MockDF for any test that would otherwise require PySpark:

class MockDF:
    def __init__(self, rows=None):
        self._rows = rows or [{"id": 1, "val": 2.0}]
    def count(self): return len(self._rows)
    def toPandas(self):
        import pandas as pd; return pd.DataFrame(self._rows)

All tests in tests/unit/ must pass without pyspark installed.

docs.title: Integration tests
docs.text:
Mark with @pytest.mark.integration and use SparkBackend:

import pytest
from ubunye.backends.spark_backend import SparkBackend

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def spark():
    with SparkBackend(app_name="test", conf={"spark.sql.shuffle.partitions": "1"}) as be:
        yield be.spark

@pytest.mark.integration
def test_hive_reader(spark):
    ...

How to run each test tier (unit, Spark, types, lint, docs, performance) and what each needs: Contributing, Run the tests.

docs.title: Orchestration exporters
docs.text:
ubunye/orchestration/:

  • base.py: OrchestratorExporter ABC with export(config_path, *, output_path, options) -> Path.
  • airflow_exporter.py: AirflowExporter, generates a DAG Python file (Airflow 2.4+ and 3) whose single BashOperator runs ubunye run ....
  • databricks_exporter.py: DatabricksExporter, generates a Databricks Jobs API spec (job.json).
  • spark_pipeline_exporter.py: SparkPipelineExporter, writes the task as a Spark Declarative Pipeline (Spark 4.1+).

Exporters are reached via ubunye export airflow|databricks|spark-pipeline. The CLI (ubunye/cli/export.py) loads the task's config.yaml, dumps the ORCHESTRATION block to a plain dict, and hands it to the exporter as options. For the Databricks exporter the nested databricks cluster block is flattened into top-level options so the exporter can splat it into new_cluster. They do not interact with the running cluster: they only produce configuration artifacts.

docs.title: Adding a new orchestration target
docs.text:
1. Subclass OrchestratorExporter and implement export(config_path, *, output_path, options).
  2. Add a new value to the OrchestrationType enum in ubunye/config/schema.py (it already lists prefect and dagster, which have no exporter yet).
  3. Export the class from ubunye/orchestration/__init__.py.
  4. Add a new Typer command in ubunye/cli/export.py that maps OrchestrationConfig fields to the exporter's options.

docs.title: Error Reference
docs.text:
Every exception Ubunye raises, for people who catch errors in Python. If you have an error message and want the fix, start at Troubleshooting instead.

Every user-facing error inherits from UbunyeError and the standard Python type it replaces, so existing except ValueError or except KeyError catches keep working.

docs.title: Catching errors
docs.text:
import ubunye
from ubunye import UbunyeError

try:
    ubunye.run_task(task_dir="pipelines/fraud/ingestion/claim_etl")
except UbunyeError as e:
    print(e)           # formatted message with context + hint
    print(e.context)   # dict of relevant facts
    print(e.hint)      # suggested fix (or None)

Narrow catches still work via dual inheritance:

except FileNotFoundError:   # catches TaskNotFoundError, RegistryNotFoundError
except KeyError:            # catches ReaderNotFoundError, WriterNotFoundError, SecretError, FeatureContractError
except ValueError:          # catches ConfigError, RegistryError subtypes, ExpectationError
except RuntimeError:        # catches SparkSessionError, ModelNotFittedError, DeployError, LLMError, RunLeaseHeld

docs.title: Exception hierarchy
docs.text:
UbunyeError(Exception)
├── ConfigError(UbunyeError, ValueError)
│   ├── ConfigFieldError          unknown config fields, with typo suggestions
│   ├── ConfigTemplateError       undefined Jinja variables, unset env variables
│   └── ConfigProfileError        a profile name the config does not define
├── TaskNotFoundError(UbunyeError, FileNotFoundError)
├── TaskClassMissingError(UbunyeError, RuntimeError)
├── PluginNotFoundError(UbunyeError, KeyError)
│   ├── ReaderNotFoundError
│   ├── WriterNotFoundError
│   ├── TransformNotFoundError
│   ├── MonitorNotFoundError
│   ├── BackendNotFoundError      no backend under that name, or it failed to load
│   └── RegistryBackendNotFoundError  no registry backend under that name, or it failed to load
├── SourceReadError(UbunyeError, IOError)
├── SinkWriteError(UbunyeError, IOError)
├── TransformOutputError(UbunyeError, TypeError)
├── SecretError(UbunyeError, KeyError)          a secret:// reference cannot be read
├── LLMError(UbunyeError, RuntimeError)         a model call fails or cannot be made
│   └── LLMBudgetError                          a call refused before sending: it could pass a limit
├── ExpectationError(UbunyeError, ValueError)   an output breaks a `fail` expectation; nothing written
├── BackendCapabilityError(UbunyeError, ValueError)  the task needs something the backend cannot do
├── SparkSessionError(UbunyeError, RuntimeError)
├── ModelLoadError(UbunyeError, ImportError)
├── ModelNotFittedError(UbunyeError, RuntimeError)
├── FeatureContractError(UbunyeError, KeyError)  at predict, the frame lacks a feature the model declared
├── RegistryError(UbunyeError, ValueError)
│   ├── VersionExistsError
│   ├── VersionNotFoundError
│   └── PromotionBlockedError
├── RegistryNotFoundError(UbunyeError, FileNotFoundError)
├── LineageRecordNotFoundError(UbunyeError, FileNotFoundError)
├── RunLeaseHeld(UbunyeError, RuntimeError)     another live run holds this task and batch
│   └── BatchFinished                           a finished run already appended this batch; --rerun replaces it
├── RunLeaseLost(UbunyeError, RuntimeError)     this run's lease was taken over; it stops
├── UpstreamNotReady(UbunyeError, RuntimeError) a task in CONFIG.requires has not succeeded for this batch
└── DeployError(UbunyeError, RuntimeError)
    ├── AuthNotFoundError         Databricks credentials are missing
    ├── AuthInvalidError          Databricks credentials are rejected
    ├── TargetNotFoundError       the deploy target is not in targets.yaml
    ├── WorkspaceUploadError      uploading files to the workspace failed
    └── BundleDeployError         creating or updating the job failed

SecretError and LLMError never carry the secret or the key. RunLeaseHeld, BatchFinished and RunLeaseLost are explained in Safe reruns; FeatureContractError in ADR 012.

docs.title: Example error output
docs.text:
Missing transformations.py

TaskNotFoundError: Missing transformations.py at pipelines/demo/etl/hello_world/transformations.py.

  Task dir:      pipelines/demo/etl/hello_world
  Expected file: pipelines/demo/etl/hello_world/transformations.py
  Hint: Run 'ubunye init' to scaffold a new task, or check the directory path.

Unknown reader format

  Format:    hve

  Installed: ['binary', 'delta', 'hive', 'jdbc', 'rest_api', 's3', 'unity']
  Hint: Check the 'format' field in CONFIG.inputs.source. Installed reader plugins: binary, delta, hive, jdbc, rest_api, s3, unity

  Available: ['DEV', 'PROD']

An undefined variable that is not under env gives Undefined variable 'name' in config value ..., with the list of variables that are available.

docs.title: Importing exceptions
docs.text:
# Broadest catch
from ubunye import UbunyeError

# By category
from ubunye.core.errors import (
    ConfigError,
    SourceReadError,
    SinkWriteError,
    TaskNotFoundError,
    ReaderNotFoundError,
)

# Also available from ubunye.core (all but SecretError, LLMError,
# LLMBudgetError and ExpectationError, which only ubunye.core.errors has)
from ubunye.core import TaskNotFoundError

# Elsewhere
from ubunye.core.runs import RunLeaseHeld, BatchFinished, RunLeaseLost
from ubunye.lineage.upstream import UpstreamNotReady
from ubunye.models.backends import RegistryBackendNotFoundError

docs.title: Interfaces (Protocol APIs)
docs.text:
A seam is a place you plug your own code in. Ubunye has five, for anyone who wants to keep models, run records, deploys or credentials somewhere Ubunye does not ship.

Each seam is a Python typing.Protocol: any class with the right methods fits, with no base class to inherit. Your class is found through an entry point (a name your package registers in its pyproject.toml).

Protocol What you plug in Entry point group Chosen by DeployAdapter A deploy adapter: sends a task to a remote platform ubunye.deploy_adapters The deploy command RegistryBackend A registry backend: where model versions and their stages live ubunye.registry_backends Name, then UBUNYE_REGISTRY_BACKEND, then filesystem RunRecordStore A run record store: where run records go ubunye.lineage_backends --lineage-backend, then UBUNYE_LINEAGE_BACKEND, then filesystem LineageBackend The older lineage backend contract, kept for code that uses it ubunye.lineage_backends As for the run record store AuthBackend An auth backend: finds and checks Databricks credentials ubunye.auth_backends The credentials that are set

These are not the same as an execution backend (spark, pandas, the engine a task runs on). That seam is a base class, not a protocol, and has its own page: Execution backends. Readers, writers and transforms are plugins too: Writing a plugin.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text: Three decisions shape how every seam behaves.

docs.title: Decision 1: Non-blocking metadata writes
docs.text:
record(), register(), and promote() send their metadata updates to a background worker thread with a bounded queue (default 1 000, UBUNYE_METADATA_QUEUE_SIZE).

  • Queue overflow: drop the oldest pending write, log a warning.
  • Shutdown: flush() drains the queue, with a timeout (default 30 s, UBUNYE_METADATA_FLUSH_TIMEOUT).
  • Artifact writes (model files) stay synchronous: the method returns only after the model is safely stored.

It uses a worker thread, not async/await, because async fights Spark's threading model in Python.

docs.title: Decision 2: Graceful degradation
docs.text:
When a metadata write fails, the run goes on and the record is kept in a local file to replay later. See Fallback manifests.

Auth is excluded: authentication failures always stop the run at once. A pipeline must not run with invalid credentials.

docs.title: Decision 3: Schema evolution
docs.text:
Every dataclass that crosses a seam separates strict core fields from a flexible metadata: Dict[str, str]:

  • Core fields never change without a major engine version bump.
  • New data goes into metadata: old clients ignore unknown keys, new clients write new keys without touching the schema.
  • Every record stamps engine_version so readers can filter by writer version.

docs.title: DeployAdapter
docs.text:
A deploy adapter sends a task's config and artifacts to a remote environment.

from ubunye.interfaces import DeployAdapter, DeployContext, DeployResult

Bases: Protocol

Structural interface for deployment backends.

Each adapter is responsible for:

  1. Validating that the target dict contains the fields it needs.
  2. Preparing artifacts (notebooks, config bundles) for the target.
  3. Uploading artifacts and creating/updating the remote job.
  4. Returning a :class:DeployResult with job metadata.

Built-in: DatabricksDeployAdapter, entry point ubunye.deploy_adapters:databricks.

docs.title: name property
docs.text:
name

Short identifier for this adapter (e.g. "databricks").

docs.title: deploy
docs.text:
deploy(ctx, target, *, dry_run=False)

Deploy a task to the target environment.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: ctx: Task metadata, config dict, and filesystem paths. target: Adapter-specific target configuration (validated by the adapter via :meth:validate_target). dry_run: If True, build and return the job spec without making any remote API calls.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: DeployResult Job metadata including name, id, spec, and workspace path.

docs.title: get_job_url
docs.text:
get_job_url(job_id, target)

Return a browser URL to the deployed job.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: job_id: The job identifier returned by :meth:deploy. target: The same target dict, which typically contains the host URL.

docs.title: validate_target
docs.text:
validate_target(target)

Validate adapter-specific target config.

docs.title: Raises
docs.text: ubunye.core.errors.TargetNotFoundError When required keys are missing or values are invalid.

docs.title: ubunye.interfaces.deploy.DeployContext dataclass
docs.text:
Structured metadata for a deploy operation.

Callers construct this from CLI flags and the parsed config; the adapter never derives task identity from filesystem paths.

docs.title: ubunye.interfaces.deploy.DeployResult dataclass
docs.text:
Returned by :meth:DeployAdapter.deploy.

metadata carries adapter-specific extras (notebook source, cluster id, etc.) without polluting the core fields.

docs.title: RegistryBackend
docs.text:
A registry backend manages model versions: register, promote, demote, delete.

from ubunye.interfaces import RegistryBackend, ModelVersionInfo

Bases: Protocol

Structural interface for model registries.

Concrete implementations: FilesystemRegistryBackend (built-in), MLflowModelRegistryBackend (mlflow, ADR 014).

Built-in:

  • FilesystemRegistryBackend, entry point ubunye.registry_backends:filesystem. Keeps models and their stages in a folder.
  • MLflowModelRegistryBackend, entry point ubunye.registry_backends:mlflow. Keeps them in the MLflow Model Registry: each Ubunye version is a registered model version, and staging and production are MLflow aliases. Needs pip install 'ubunye-engine[ml]'. See ADR 014.

MLflowRegistryBackend (a folder, with runs logged to MLflow on top, best effort, never blocking the pipeline) is deprecated since 0.9 and still works; use MLflowModelRegistryBackend.

Which one is used: the name you give (ubunye models --backend, or backend: in the config's registry block), else UBUNYE_REGISTRY_BACKEND, else filesystem. Ubunye does not guess from the host: on Databricks, set UBUNYE_REGISTRY_BACKEND=mlflow if you want MLflow. Why: ADR 010.

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
delete(*, use_case, model_name, version)

Remove a version and its artifacts.

docs.title: demote
docs.text:
demote(*, use_case, model_name, version, to_stage)

Demote a version to a lower stage.

Never move a version up: refuse (RegistryError) a move to production, or to staging from below. Call :func:ubunye.models.lifecycle.check_demote first.

docs.title: get
docs.text:
get(*, use_case, model_name, version=None, stage=None)

Retrieve a model version by exact version or active stage.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: tuple of (artifact_path, ModelVersionInfo) artifact_path is an opaque string — it may be a local path, an MLflow artifact URI, or a cloud storage URL. Callers pass it to ModelClass.load(artifact_path).

docs.title: Raises
docs.text: ubunye.core.errors.VersionNotFoundError When no matching version exists.

docs.title: list_versions
docs.text:
list_versions(*, use_case, model_name)

List all registered versions, newest first.

docs.title: promote
docs.text:
promote(*, use_case, model_name, version, to_stage, gates=None, promoted_by=None)

Promote a version to a higher lifecycle stage.

If gates are provided, all checks must pass before the transition. On gate failure, raises :class:~ubunye.core.errors.PromotionBlockedError — this is NOT caught by the graceful degradation layer (auth and gate failures must propagate).

Metadata update is non-blocking per Decision 1.

docs.title: register
docs.text:
register(*, use_case, model_name, version, model, metrics, metadata=None, lineage_run_id=None)

Register a trained model as a new version.

Artifact writes are synchronous — the method returns only after the model is safely persisted. Index/metadata updates are non-blocking per Decision 1.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: use_case: Logical namespace (e.g. "fraud_detection"). model_name: Model identifier within the use case. version: Explicit semver string, or None for auto-increment. model: A trained model instance whose save()/metadata() methods will be called by the backend. metrics: Training metrics dict. metadata: Optional flexible key-value pairs (Decision 3). lineage_run_id: Optional lineage run ID for cross-referencing.

docs.title: ubunye.interfaces.registry.ModelVersionInfo dataclass
docs.text:
Cross-boundary model version record (Decision 3 compliant).

Core fields are strict; everything else goes into metadata. Every record stamps engine_version so downstream consumers can filter by writer version.

docs.title: RunRecordStore
docs.text:
A run record store keeps run records (the whole RunContext, what lineage show prints). Every store in ubunye.lineage_backends provides it. No base class needed.

from ubunye.interfaces import RunRecordStore

Bases: Protocol

Where run records live (ADR 011). Four methods, no base class needed.

A task is named by its task_path, "usecase/package/task". Newest first means the record written last comes first. A store is built with one argument, its location (a directory, a table name, a URL), given unchanged.

Built-in:

  • FileSystemLineageStore, entry point ubunye.lineage_backends:filesystem. One JSON file per run. Uses a run_id to path index for fast lookups and an in-memory RunContext cache to avoid parsing JSON again on search.
  • DeltaLineageBackend, entry point ubunye.lineage_backends:delta. Stores each run record whole (JSON plus index columns) in a Delta table or path, through the active SparkSession or a local one it starts. Like every store, a record it cannot write goes to a fallback manifest, with a warning.

Which one is used: --lineage-backend (or lineage_backend= in Python), else UBUNYE_LINEAGE_BACKEND, else filesystem. Where each keeps its records: Where run records are stored. Why: ADR 011.

Prove a store keeps the contract with the shipped suite:

import pytest

from ubunye.testing.lineage_conformance import LineageStoreConformance


class TestMyStore(LineageStoreConformance):
    @pytest.fixture
    def store(self, tmp_path):
        return MyStore(str(tmp_path / "runs"))

docs.title: LineageBackend
docs.text:
The older lineage contract: record, search, compact, over a flat LineageRecord. Kept for code that uses it; no run record is stored through it, since a LineageRecord keeps only a few fields of one.

from ubunye.interfaces import LineageBackend, LineageRecord

Bases: Protocol

Structural interface for lineage storage backends.

Concrete implementations: FilesystemLineageBackend (built-in), DeltaLineageBackend (Phase 2).

Built-in: the same two classes as the run record store. The Delta one's older LineageRecord methods still use JSON files when no SparkSession existed when it was built, and log that.

A store's save raises when it cannot write. The recorder then keeps the record in the fallback manifest, with a warning naming the ubunye sync lineage command that replays it. This is the same for every store.

Persist a lineage record (non-blocking per Decision 1).

Creates or overwrites the record for the given run_id. Typically called twice per task: once at start (status="running") and once at end (status="success" or "error").

The actual write is dispatched to a background worker thread. On failure, the record is written to a fallback manifest (Decision 2).

docs.title: AuthBackend
docs.text:
An auth backend finds and checks Databricks credentials.

from ubunye.interfaces import AuthBackend, Credentials

Bases: Protocol

Structural interface for authentication backends.

Concrete implementations: TokenAuthBackend (built-in), ServicePrincipalAuthBackend (Phase 2).

Built-in:

  • TokenAuthBackend, entry point ubunye.auth_backends:token. Reads the token from DATABRICKS_TOKEN (or the env var named by token_env in targets.yaml).
  • ServicePrincipalAuthBackend, entry point ubunye.auth_backends:service_principal. Uses DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID + DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET for OAuth M2M auth.

Which one is used:

Set in the environment Auth backend DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID and DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET service_principal (wins when both kinds are set) DATABRICKS_TOKEN token Neither Raises AuthNotFoundError

See Databricks authentication.

Every group the engine reads, with what it ships. Third-party packages add their own classes under these groups in their pyproject.toml.

Group What it holds Built-in names ubunye.deploy_adapters Deploy adapters databricks (DatabricksDeployAdapter) ubunye.registry_backends Registry backends filesystem (FilesystemRegistryBackend), mlflow (MLflowModelRegistryBackend) ubunye.lineage_backends Run record stores filesystem (FileSystemLineageStore), delta (DeltaLineageBackend) ubunye.auth_backends Auth backends token (TokenAuthBackend), service_principal (ServicePrincipalAuthBackend) ubunye.artifact_stores Where model files go, by URL scheme file (LocalArtifactStore); a third party adds a scheme here ubunye.backends Execution backends (Execution backends) spark, databricks, pandas ubunye.readers Readers (format: of an input) hive, jdbc, s3, delta, binary, unity, rest_api ubunye.writers Writers (format: of an output) s3, delta, hive, jdbc, unity, rest_api ubunye.transforms Transforms noop, model ubunye.ml Model wrappers sklearn, sparkml ubunye.monitors Monitors (older than hooks) mlflow, lineage ubunye.hooks Hooks, always on events, otel, prometheus ubunye.secrets Secret providers for secret:// (Secrets) env, file, databricks, aws-sm, gcp-sm, azure-kv ubunye.llm_backends Model call providers (LLM calls) anthropic, openai_compatible, databricks_serving

How to write and register readers, writers and transforms: Writing a plugin.

docs.title: Fallback manifests and ubunye sync
docs.text:
When a metadata write fails (a run record, or a model registry update), the run goes on, and the record is appended to a local fallback manifest:

~/.ubunye/fallback/{run_id}/{kind}.jsonl

kind is lineage or registry. Each line is a JSON object with all record fields plus a _fallback_at timestamp. The run logs a warning that says so.

Replay them once the store is back:

ubunye sync lineage                    # replay all run record manifests
ubunye sync lineage --run-id abc123    # replay one run
ubunye sync lineage --lineage-backend delta --lineage-dir main.ops.ubunye_runs
ubunye sync registry                   # replay all registry manifests

Replay skips records already written (the key is run_id + task + recorded_at), so running it twice is safe. Replayed manifests are moved to ~/.ubunye/fallback/synced/. Every flag: ubunye sync.

docs.title: Writing your own
docs.text:
1. Implement the protocol methods (no base class needed).

  2. Register the entry point in your pyproject.toml:

    [project.entry-points."ubunye.lineage_backends"]
my_store = "my_package.lineage:MyRunRecordStore"

  3. Install the package (pip install -e .).

  4. The engine finds it by name. A run record store is then used with --lineage-backend my_store (or UBUNYE_LINEAGE_BACKEND=my_store), and built with one argument, --lineage-dir as given:

    from ubunye.lineage import stores

store = stores.open_store("my-location", "my_store")

A registry backend is used with ubunye models --backend my_registry (or UBUNYE_REGISTRY_BACKEND=my_registry).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Something went wrong and you want it fixed. Each entry starts with what you see, then says why it happens and what to do. For what each exception class means, see the Error Reference.

docs.title: First step: ask ubunye doctor
docs.text:
ubunye doctor checks this machine (Python, Java, the backends, the plugins) and, given a task, the environment variables and secret providers its config needs. It says what would fail and how to fix it:

ubunye doctor -d pipelines -u demo -p starter -t filter_adults

[OK] python: Python 3.13.18 on linux
[OK] ubunye-engine: 0.9.0
[WARN] java: pyspark is installed but no Java was found (JAVA_HOME or java on PATH)
       fix: Spark 4 runs on Java 17 or 21; Spark 3.5 on Java 8, 11 or 17. Install one, or run with --backend pandas.
[OK] delta-spark: delta-spark 4.4.1 with Spark 4.2.0
[OK] backend: databricks: usable, needs Java, distributed
[OK] backend: pandas: usable, single machine
[WARN] backend: spark (default): Spark needs Java, and none was found (JAVA_HOME or java on PATH).
[WARN] default backend: a run without --backend uses 'spark', which cannot run here (on Databricks the platform's own backend is used instead)
       fix: Pass --backend pandas, or install what 'spark' needs.
[OK] plugins: 18 load
[OK] task filter_adults: environment: every variable it needs is set
[FAIL] task filter_adults: secret provider aws-sm: needs boto3
       fix: pip install boto3
[OK] task filter_adults: config: loads and validates

4 to look at; a run would fail.

This machine has no Java, and the task reads a password from AWS Secrets Manager without the AWS client installed. It exits 1 when a run would fail.

ubunye plan then checks the task itself without moving any data. Most problems below show up in one of these two first.

docs.title: Profile 'DEV' not found
docs.text:
What you see when you run a task:

ConfigProfileError: Profile 'DEV' not found.

  Profile:   DEV
  Available: ['dev']
  Hint: Valid profiles: dev

Why. ubunye run uses the profile DEV when you give no -m. Profile names are matched exactly, case included, and this config's profile is spelled dev. (A long traceback may print above the message; the last lines are the part that matters.)

Fix. Either rename the profile in config.yaml to DEV, or pass the name as written: ubunye run ... -m dev. Use upper case names (DEV, PROD) to match the default. A config with no profiles at all runs under any -m. Note that ubunye export airflow and ubunye export databricks default to --profile prod, so pass --profile PROD if your profile is upper case. See Engine and Profiles.

docs.title: Spark cannot find Java
docs.text:
What you see when you run on Spark (no --backend pandas):

JAVA_HOME is not set
...
PySparkRuntimeError: [JAVA_GATEWAY_EXITED] Java gateway process exited before
sending its port number.

Why. Spark runs on Java, and none was found on PATH or through JAVA_HOME.

Fix. Install a Java version your Spark supports (the versions are on Installation) and check it with java -version. Or run without Java on pandas: add --backend pandas.

docs.title: The pandas backend cannot serve hive, jdbc, unity or delta
docs.text:
What you see from ubunye plan --backend pandas:

  problem: input 'people' uses the 'hive' connector, which needs spark; the pandas backend does not provide it.

Plan would fail: 1 problem(s) in 1 task(s).

and from ubunye run --backend pandas:

  - input 'people' uses the 'hive' connector, which needs spark; the pandas
backend does not provide it.

  Backend: pandas
  Hint: Run it on a backend that can (--backend spark), or change the inputs and
outputs listed above.

Why. On pandas, only the s3 (files on any path, local or cloud) and rest_api connectors work. hive, jdbc, unity and delta need Spark. The same check refuses a file option pandas does not support.

Fix. Run on Spark (leave out --backend pandas), or read files with format: s3. See Execution Backends.

docs.title: Warning: --package is renamed --pipeline
docs.text:
What you see:

Warning: --package is renamed --pipeline; it will be removed in 1.0.

Why. In 0.9 the middle folder level is called a pipeline, so -p is now short for --pipeline. The old --package still works until 1.0. Giving both is an error:

Invalid value for '--pipeline': give the pipeline once: use -p/--pipeline
and drop --package (its old name).

Fix. Write -p or --pipeline in your scripts and jobs. In Python, use run_pipeline(pipeline=...). See Upgrading.

docs.title: Run refused: the batch already landed
docs.text:
What you see when you run an appending task a second time with the same -dt:

[ERROR] Run refused for filter_adults: demo/starter/filter_adults already finished this batch (run b88e7ba8 (finished 2026-11-10T10:36:38Z)) and appends to adults: running it again would add the batch twice.

  Finished: .../pipelines/.ubunye/leases/demo/starter/filter_adults/ecdf848508a4535d.finished.json
  Hint: To replace the batch, run again with --rerun (rerun=True in Python). If each run adds new data to the same batch, give each run its own variable, for example --var hour=13.

Why. A batch is the task with its -dt and --var values. This one was already appended by a run that finished, and running it again would write the same rows twice.

Fix. Choose one:

  • To replace the batch: add --rerun. You will see Replaced the batch: removed 1 file(s) of the earlier run.
  • If each run really adds new data: give each run its own variable, for example --var hour=13.
  • To finish a pipeline that stopped half way: add --resume. Tasks that finished the batch are skipped.

See Safe Reruns.

docs.title: Unknown field 'ENGNE'
docs.text:
What you see:

[ERROR] Config validation failed for 'filter_adults':
Unknown fields in pipelines/demo/starter/filter_adults/config.yaml:

  (top level):
    Unknown field 'ENGNE'
    Did you mean 'ENGINE'?

Why. A key in config.yaml is misspelled. Ubunye refuses keys it does not know, so a typo cannot be silently ignored.

Fix. Use the spelling it suggests. ubunye validate finds these without running anything. See Config Overview.

docs.title: A secret provider package is missing
docs.text:
What you see when a config uses, for example, secret://aws-sm/...:

SecretError: Could not read secret secret://aws-sm/prod/shop-db#password:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'boto3'

  Provider:  aws-sm
  Reference: prod/shop-db#password
  Hint: pip install 'ubunye-engine[aws]'; the login is the AWS SDK's (profile,
role, env).

Why. Each cloud secret store needs its own client library, and it is not installed.

Fix. Install the extra the hint names: [aws] for aws-sm, [gcp] for gcp-sm, [azure] for azure-kv, [databricks] for databricks outside a cluster. ubunye doctor with a task finds this before a run. See Secrets.

docs.title: PySpark does not yet fully support pandas >= 3.0.0
docs.text:
What you see when Spark starts:

FutureWarning: PySpark does not yet fully support pandas >= 3.0.0. Some features may not work correctly. It is recommended to use pandas < 3.0.0 for now.

Why. You installed the pandas and spark extras together and pip chose pandas 3. PySpark prints this warning for any pandas 3.

Fix. Nothing to fix: it is expected and the run carries on. To silence it, install "pandas<3". See Installation.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
• Every exception class, with what it means: Error Reference.
  • Every command and flag: CLI Reference.
  • Ask, or report a bug, on GitHub.

docs.title: Upgrading from 0.8 to 0.9
docs.text:
What to change in your commands, configs and Python code when you move from Ubunye Engine 0.8 to 0.9. Most projects need only the first section. Everything new is listed in the Changelog.

pip install --upgrade "ubunye-engine[pandas]"   # or the extras you use
ubunye version                                  # Ubunye Engine v0.9.0

docs.title: 1. --package is now -p/--pipeline
docs.text:
The middle folder level (use case, pipeline, task) is called a pipeline everywhere now. Every command that took -p/--package takes -p/--pipeline.

0.8 0.9 ubunye run -d pipelines -u fraud -p etl -t claims the same: -p still works ubunye run -d pipelines -u fraud --package etl -t claims ubunye run -d pipelines -u fraud --pipeline etl -t claims ubunye.run_pipeline("pipelines", "fraud", package="etl", tasks=["claims"]) ubunye.run_pipeline("pipelines", "fraud", pipeline="etl", tasks=["claims"]) ubunye.api.job_health(..., package="etl") ubunye.api.job_health(..., pipeline="etl")

The old names keep working until 1.0:

  • --package is hidden from --help and prints one warning: Warning: --package is renamed --pipeline; it will be removed in 1.0.
  • Giving both --package and --pipeline is an error (exit 2).
  • In Python, package= gives a DeprecationWarning; giving both pipeline= and package= raises TypeError. The order of run_pipeline()'s positional arguments is unchanged, so run_pipeline("pipelines", "fraud", "etl") still works.
  • The MCP health tool takes pipeline and still accepts package.
  • Run records keep their field named package. It holds the pipeline name.

docs.title: 2. Behaviour changes
docs.text:
Check these if they touch your project.

replace_where on an append now takes effect. Before 0.9 it was ignored on an append. Now, on a Delta or JDBC append, each run replaces that batch's rows in one step, so a retry or --rerun writes the corrected batch instead of adding it twice:

outputs:
  sales:
    format: delta
    path: /data/sales
    mode: append
    replace_where: "month = '{{ dt }}'"

A Delta append of a named batch with no replace_where now lands once: a retry adds nothing. See Safe Reruns and the replace_where sections of Files and Delta and JDBC.

ubunye models demote only moves a version down. --to takes development, staging or archived (and staging only from production). To put a version in production, use promote, which checks its gates:

0.8 0.9 ubunye models demote -u fraud -m claims_model -s .ubunye/model_store -v 3 --to production ubunye models promote -u fraud -m claims_model -s .ubunye/model_store -v 3 --to production

models promote --to takes only staging or production. A wrong --to is a usage error (exit 2) that lists the choices.

--backend mlflow now uses the MLflow Model Registry. Each version is a registered MLflow model version, and staging and production are MLflow aliases, so models:/<name>@production works. In 0.8 this backend kept models in a folder. Point it at MLflow with MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI (and MLFLOW_REGISTRY_URI if different). See Model Registry.

The registry backend is not picked from the host. The order is: the name you ask for (--backend on ubunye models, registry.backend in a model transform), else UBUNYE_REGISTRY_BACKEND, else filesystem. If you relied on MLflow being chosen on Databricks, set UBUNYE_REGISTRY_BACKEND=mlflow.
