docs.title: What the run records tell you
docs.text:
With --lineage, each run leaves a run record. A run record is about whole tables, not single documents: for each input and output it keeps the location, the row count and a hash (a fingerprint) of the data, plus a hash of your code.

ubunye lineage list  -d pipelines -u rag -p embed -t chunks
ubunye lineage trace -d pipelines -u rag -p embed -t chunks

Lineage trace: rag/embed/chunks
Run:     3c9707b4-be1d-4107-bca9-d610880fa800  [success]  2026-11-10T10:40:51
Version: etl v1.0.0

  INPUTS
    [s3] chunks
      location : lake/rag/chunks
      rows     : 6
      ...
  OUTPUTS
    [s3] embedded_chunks
      location : lake/rag/embedded_chunks
      rows     : 6
      ...

So the run record answers "which version of the chunks table made this embeddings table, with which code?". To answer "which article did this chunk come from?", use the doc_id column, which every step keeps.

docs.title: Run it every night
docs.text:
Add an ORCHESTRATION block to each task and export it as an Airflow DAG (a scheduled job). The keys and the export command are on Orchestration.

ubunye export airflow -c pipelines/rag/ingest/documents/config.yaml -o dags/rag_ingest.py
ubunye export airflow -c pipelines/rag/chunk/documents/config.yaml  -o dags/rag_chunk.py
ubunye export airflow -c pipelines/rag/embed/chunks/config.yaml     -o dags/rag_embed.py

docs.title: Pattern: REST API Ingestion
docs.text:
For anyone who needs to pull data from a web API (a shop, a CRM, an exchange rate service) into their lake on a schedule. Each section is one common case, with a config you can copy.

  • The problem: the data you need sits behind an HTTP API, spread over many pages, behind a token, with rate limits.
  • When to use it: the API returns JSON and you want it as a table. No code is needed for the request itself: the rest_api connector does the paging, the login and the retries.
  • The one command: ubunye run -d pipelines -u shop -p ingest -t orders --lineage

Every rest_api key is listed on REST API Connector. This page shows how to put them together.

docs.title: A full example you can run
docs.text:
A task that reads every order from a shop API, a page of 3 at a time, and lands them as Parquet:

pipelines/                    # the pipelines folder (-d)
└── shop/                     # use case
    └── ingest/               # pipeline
        └── orders/           # task
            ├── config.yaml
            └── transformations.py

# pipelines/shop/ingest/orders/config.yaml
MODEL: etl
VERSION: "1.0.0"

CONFIG:
  inputs:
    orders:
      format: rest_api
      url: "{{ env.SHOP_API | default('https://api.shop.example.com') }}/v1/orders"
      auth:
        type: api_key_header
        header: X-Shop-Access-Token
        key: "secret://env/SHOP_TOKEN"
      params:
        limit: 3                # the API's own page size parameter
      pagination:
        type: offset
        page_size: 3
        max_pages: 200
      response:
        root_key: orders
      schema:
        - name: id
          type: long
        - name: created_at
          type: string          # text; convert it in the transform
        - name: total_price
          type: double
        - name: currency
          type: string
        - name: status
          type: string

  outputs:
    raw_orders:
      format: s3
      path: lake/shop/raw_orders
      file_format: parquet
      mode: overwrite

# pipelines/shop/ingest/orders/transformations.py
from ubunye.core.interfaces import Task


class IngestOrders(Task):
    def transform(self, sources: dict) -> dict:
        return {"raw_orders": sources["orders"]}
  • auth sends the token in the X-Shop-Access-Token header. The token comes from the SHOP_TOKEN environment variable through a secret reference, so it is never in the file, the plan or the run record.
  • pagination: offset asks for offset=0, then 3, then 6, until a page comes back empty.
  • schema fixes the column types, so an empty or odd page cannot change them.

Check it, then run it:

export SHOP_TOKEN=...        # your token
ubunye plan -d pipelines -u shop -p ingest -t orders --backend pandas
ubunye run  -d pipelines -u shop -p ingest -t orders --backend pandas --lineage

What success looks like (here against a small local test server that holds 7 orders, with SHOP_API pointing at it):

Task shop/ingest/orders   (backend: pandas)
  Inputs
    orders       rest_api       http://127.0.0.1:38031/v1/orders
                 not checked (not a local path)
  Transform  IngestOrders  (transformations.py)
  Outputs
    raw_orders   s3 parquet     lake/shop/raw_orders
                 mode overwrite

Plan OK: 1 task(s) can run.
Starting task: orders (Mode: DEV, Deploy: client)
[OK] Run complete for orders

lake/shop/raw_orders holds all 7 orders from the 3 pages:

 id           created_at  total_price currency   status
  1 2026-11-01T09:01:00Z        120.5      ZAR     paid
  2 2026-11-01T09:02:00Z        241.0      ZAR     paid
  3 2026-11-02T09:03:00Z        361.5      ZAR refunded
  4 2026-11-02T09:04:00Z        482.0      ZAR     paid
  5 2026-11-02T09:05:00Z        602.5      ZAR     paid
  6 2026-11-03T09:06:00Z        723.0      ZAR refunded
  7 2026-11-03T09:07:00Z        843.5      ZAR     paid

ubunye lineage trace -d pipelines -u shop -p ingest -t orders shows the API as the input, with rows : 7. A wrong token fails the run at once:

[ERROR] Run failed for orders: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url: http://127.0.0.1:38031/v1/orders?limit=3&offset=0

The same task runs on Spark with no change: drop --backend pandas.

docs.title: Single request
docs.text:
For a small answer that fits in one response, leave pagination out:

MODEL: etl
VERSION: "1.0.0"

CONFIG:
  inputs:
    exchange_rates:
      format: rest_api
      url: "https://api.exchangerate.host/latest"
      params:
        base: USD
        symbols: EUR,GBP,ZAR,JPY
      response:
        root_key: rates

  outputs:
    rates:
      format: delta
      path: s3://datalake/forex/rates/
      mode: append

docs.title: Incremental ingestion (cursor / date filter)
docs.text:
Fetch only what changed since the last run: pass the last-seen date as a variable with --var, and use it in the config with Jinja:

ubunye run -d pipelines -u crm -p ingest -t contacts \
    --var since=2026-11-01 \
    -m PROD \
    --lineage

CONFIG:
  inputs:
    contacts:
      format: rest_api
      url: "https://crm.example.com/api/contacts"
      params:
        updated_after: "{{ since | default('2020-01-01') }}"
      auth:
        type: bearer
        token: "secret://env/CRM_TOKEN"
      pagination:
        type: next_link
        next_key: next          # a top level key of the response; dotted paths are not read
      response:
        root_key: contacts

docs.title: Cursor-based pagination
docs.text:
For APIs that return a cursor/token to request the next page:

CONFIG:
  inputs:
    events:
      format: rest_api
      url: "https://api.mixpanel.com/export/events"
      auth:
        type: basic
        username: "{{ env.MP_USER }}"
        password: "secret://env/MP_SECRET"
      pagination:
        type: cursor
        cursor_response_key: next_page_token
        cursor_param: page_token

docs.title: Rate-limited API
docs.text:
For APIs with strict rate limits:

CONFIG:
  inputs:
    github_repos:
      format: rest_api
      url: "https://api.github.com/orgs/my-org/repos"
      auth:
        type: bearer
        token: "secret://env/GITHUB_TOKEN"
      headers:
        X-GitHub-Api-Version: "2022-11-28"
      pagination:
        type: next_link
        next_key: next            # from the response body; the Link header is not read
      rate_limit:
        requests_per_second: 1    # GitHub: 5000 req/hr authenticated
        retry_on: [429, 503]
        max_retries: 5

docs.title: POST with body
docs.text:
For APIs that require POST requests:

CONFIG:
  inputs:
    search_results:
      format: rest_api
      url: "https://api.elastic.example.com/search"
      method: POST
      auth:
        type: bearer
        token: "secret://env/ES_TOKEN"
      body:                     # sent as the JSON body; params would go in the URL
        query: "fraud risk"
        size: 100

docs.title: Writing back to an API
docs.text:
After enrichment, send results back to an external system:

CONFIG:
  outputs:
    scored_customers:
      format: rest_api
      url: "https://crm.example.com/api/bulk/scores"
      method: POST
      auth:
        type: bearer
        token: "secret://env/CRM_TOKEN"
      batch_size: 200
      rate_limit:
        requests_per_second: 10
        retry_on: [429, 503]
        max_retries: 3

docs.title: Handling nested JSON
docs.text:
The response.root_key only extracts one level (see Response extraction). For deeply nested responses, use a transform to flatten:

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from ubunye.core.interfaces import Task

class FlattenTask(Task):
    def transform(self, sources: dict) -> dict:
        df = sources["api_data"]
        flat = df.select(
            "id",
            F.col("address.street").alias("street"),
            F.col("address.city").alias("city"),
            F.col("metadata.tags").alias("tags"),
            F.explode("line_items").alias("item"),
        ).select("id", "street", "city", "tags", "item.*")
        return {"api_data": flat}

docs.title: Scheduling
docs.text:
Run nightly via Airflow. Every key and flag is on Orchestration:

ORCHESTRATION:
  type: airflow
  schedule: "0 4 * * *"
  retries: 3
  tags: [rest_api, ingestion, crm]

ubunye export airflow \
    -c pipelines/crm/ingest/contacts/config.yaml \
    -o dags/crm_contacts.py --profile PROD

docs.title: The proving ground
docs.text:
Ubunye says a task runs the same on a laptop, on Spark, on Databricks and on the clouds. The proving ground is how that stops being a claim: the same workload (a fixed task with fixed data) is run in each place, and the run records are compared, dimension by dimension. An environment that did not run says so. This page explains how; the numbers are in Latest results. To try it yourself, follow Tutorial 1.

The latest cloud results were measured with engine 0.7.2. Engine 0.9.0 has not been re-run on the clouds yet; locally, C01 gives the same digest on pandas and Spark with 0.9.0.

docs.title: The contract
docs.text:
For one workload, every environment is compared with a reference environment:

Dimension PASS means Compared from the record execute the run succeeded status identity it is the same workload code_hash, and the same output names inputs every input held the same rows each input's data_hash, where inputs were hashed data every output holds the same rows each output's data_hash (rows-v1), same hash_method schema every output has the same columns and types each output's schema_hash (canonical type names) rows every output has the same number of rows each output's row_count

rows-v1 covers every row, ignores row and column order, writes timestamps as UTC instants and tells null from NaN, so data PASS is semantic equality of the rows and their types.

Verdicts: PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL (some of it could not be compared, such as a record without a hash or hashed by an older method), NOT RECORDED, and for an environment that did not execute, NOT RUN or UNSUPPORTED. An environment that was expected and left no evidence is NOT RUN, never PASS.

Not compared, on purpose: the config hash (it covers paths, and a cloud reads s3:// where a laptop reads a folder), and the bytes of written files (Spark and pandas write valid Parquet differently; byte equality is not a promise Ubunye makes).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
# after a run with --lineage, turn its record into an observation
ubunye prove observe --workload c01-portable-etl --env spark-local \
  -d pipelines -u proving -p c01 -t etl -o evidence

# several tasks: one observation each, named <workload>-<task> (r2-olist-clean, ...)
ubunye prove observe --workload r2-olist --env pandas-local \
  -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t clean -t orders_fact -t monthly -o evidence

# a record from elsewhere (a cloud run's artifact)
ubunye prove observe --workload c01-portable-etl --env aws-glue --kind cloud \
  --provider aws --runtime "Glue 5.0" --record glue.json -o evidence

# an environment that did not run, and why
ubunye prove skip --workload c01-portable-etl --env azure --reason "no subscription" -o evidence

# compare everything with the reference; exit 1 if any executed environment disagrees
ubunye prove report evidence --workload c01-portable-etl --reference spark-local \
  --expect pandas-local,databricks,aws-glue,gcp-dataproc,azure --json m.json --md m.md

An observation is one JSON file, evidence/<workload>/<environment>.json: the run record, the platform, the cost with where the figure came from (actual, provider_estimate, ubunye_estimate, local or unknown; an estimate is never shown as a bill), and a link to the run.

docs.title: Workloads
docs.text: Id What it protects Where c01-portable-etl a portable (Narwhals) join, filter, null group keys, integer money, timestamps cut to a day examples/proving/c01_portable_etl; PASS on pandas, local Spark, Kubernetes (kind), AWS Glue 5.0, GCP Dataproc Serverless, Azure Container Apps and Databricks serverless, one digest (latest) r1-food-prices-clean, r1-food-prices-monitor a real two step pipeline (WFP food prices in Africa): a folder of CSV files with a declared schema, units turned into a price per kg, expectations, a monthly table and alerts; the second step reads what the first wrote examples/real-world/food_prices_africa (committed sample); both steps in one launch per environment, each compared on its own; PASS on the same seven environments, digests f61e0f0544f5 and 021cc19ca2b6 (latest) r2-olist-clean, r2-olist-orders_fact, r2-olist-monthly a three step pipeline over nine joined tables (Olist e-commerce): input contracts on raw CSV files, quarantine, reconcile (rows and money sums) and a warning, a CSV with a byte order mark and one with text over several lines examples/real-world/olist_ecommerce (committed synthetic sample); all three steps in one launch per environment; PASS on the same seven environments, digests 6affe2f5382c, 6dcf270328d8 and a0bd206029ca (latest)

docs.title: What is not proven yet
docs.text: Hadoop/YARN and EMR Serverless have no proving run yet, so the docs do not claim them. Neither is claimed until a run says so.

docs.title: What it has found
docs.text:
Each problem the proving ground found was fixed in the engine:

  • A Spark session's day depended on the machine's time zone. Spark now runs in UTC unless you set a zone, and the report fails a run set to a different zone. Why it works this way: ADR 007.
  • A cloud run's record was lost when the cloud's log store cut a long line, and again when it cut a line inside the record's start or end marker.
  • A deploy ran only one task per launch; it now runs every -t in order in one launch.
  • Expectations (data checks) on Spark needed pyarrow, which the Spark images lack.
  • A failed Kubernetes Job held the deploy for its whole timeout.

Why it works this way: ADR 006 (the run record that is compared).

docs.title: Proving ground: latest results
docs.text:
The same workloads, run in seven environments and compared with local Spark. Every row below passed. How the comparison works: The proving ground.

Which engine version was proven

These results were measured with engine 0.7.2 (the Engine column), on 2026-09-30. Engine 0.9.0 has not been re-run on the clouds yet. Locally, with 0.9.0, C01 gives the same digest, bb08a7d7a9fd, on pandas and on local Spark.

Where the numbers come from: ubunye prove report in ubunye-infra (workflow prove.yml), engine branch hardening/real-world at commit bbb56bb, 2026-09-30, after the fixes of that day. C01 comes from prove-c01 run 36709022623, R1 from prove-r1 run 36709026536, R2 from prove-r2 run 36709032414. The machine-readable results are c01-portable-etl.json, r1-food-prices-clean.json, r1-food-prices-monitor.json, r2-olist-clean.json, r2-olist-orders_fact.json and r2-olist-monthly.json. The run records of each environment stay in the runs' artifacts, because they carry storage paths.

R1 (examples/real-world/food_prices_africa, the committed sample) runs clean then monitor in one launch per environment (ubunye deploy -t clean -t monitor). So on Kubernetes and Container Apps, monitor reads what clean wrote to the container's own disk. Each step is compared on its own, so three things are proven: the in-between output (prices_per_kg, 2,229 rows), the monthly table (47 rows) and the alerts (2 rows: Chad, January 2026, imported rice +59% and wheat flour +78%, 54 markets each). The digests are the example's golden digests in tests/unit/examples/test_food_prices_example.py.

R2 (examples/real-world/olist_ecommerce, a synthetic sample shaped like the Olist files) runs clean, orders_fact and monthly in one launch per environment, with input contracts, quarantine and reconcile on every step. The digests are the example's golden digests in tests/unit/examples/test_olist_example.py.

Databricks runs as a service principal (OAuth machine to machine), not a user token. Cloud cost is unknown: no billing figure was collected yet.

docs.title: Proving ground: the state it starts from
Proving ground: the state it starts from
docs.text:
History

This is the audit as of 2026-09-28, engine 0.7.1. Many gaps listed here are now closed: each gap below says which. For today's results see Latest results.

Audited 2026-09-28 against the code, not the docs: engine hardening/real-world at fa1b456 (main is v0.7.1, the latest release and PyPI version), ubunye-infra main, ubunye-examples main. The claim being built toward: the same logical workload runs on different engines, machines and clouds, and Ubunye's own evidence says whether the result stayed equivalent.

docs.title: The evidence Ubunye already produces
docs.text: The run record (ADR 006, record v2) is already the right unit of proof. Per run it keeps the engine version, backend, variables, config_hash, code_hash, environment and its hash, per-step timings, and for every input and output a data_hash (rows-v1: every row, order and timezone free, types by one set of names, the same on Spark and pandas), a schema_hash from the same canonical types, and the row count. ubunye gate compares two records rule by rule. The proving ground builds on these; it does not introduce a second truth.

docs.title: What is proven, and where the proof lives
docs.text:
Environment Workload Evidence Machine-readable pandas and Spark, local integration tier: test_the_same_task_leaves_the_same_receipt_on_both_engines, test_same_task_same_data_on_spark_and_pandas; examples titanic_local, titanic_multitask_local (same_receipt.sh) CI, pairwise test result only AWS Glue 5.0 11_run_anywhere (examples repo) infra deploy-live artifact glue-record (run record) yes GCP Dataproc Serverless 2.2 same infra deploy-live artifact dataproc-record yes Kubernetes (kind) same infra containers-live artifact k8s-record yes Azure Container Apps same infra containers-live artifact aca-record yes Databricks serverless same infra databricks-rc: hashes asserted in the log no Spark Declarative Pipelines same infra sdp-live: log no local, Docker, kind, s3a, spark-submit same examples portability.yml: a separate fingerprint (067da98e...), equal to each other, no reference no EMR Serverless built, never run (the AWS free plan blocks EMR) none no

All cloud runs so far used engine 0.7.0 on 2026-09-24/25 and agree: documents 2200b9e5..., document_chunks 95c977d2....

docs.title: Gaps this programme starts from
docs.text:
1. No joined result. Each workflow compares itself with a hard-coded value or one other environment; nothing gathers all environments into one comparison, and nothing says NOT RUN for an environment that did not run. Closed: ubunye prove report compares every environment with one reference and marks a missing one NOT RUN (the proving ground).
  2. Two truths. The examples' platforms/fingerprint.py hashes Delta tables its own way; the engine's receipt hash is the one ADR 006 defends. The proving ground uses the receipt. Closed for the proving ground: it compares only the run record's hashes.
  3. Logs are not evidence. Databricks and SDP print hashes; they should upload the record. Closed: Databricks now uploads its run record and is compared like every other environment (latest).
  4. One cloud workload, and it is Spark-only. 11_run_anywhere writes Delta; there is no workload proven on pandas and on the clouds alike. Closed: C01, R1 and R2 are portable and PASS on pandas, local Spark and five cloud or container environments (latest).
  5. No teardown. Glue and Container Apps jobs and pushed images are kept and reused (idle cost near zero, images cost storage); staged data is cleared before a run, not after. Closed: after the 2026-09-29 runs, a check of every cloud found no job, stored object, image or workspace folder left from either workload.
  6. Credentials: AWS, GCP and Azure sandboxes use OIDC; Databricks uses a stored token (migration path: Databricks OIDC federation for GitHub Actions); the examples repo's cloud jobs use stored keys and are skipped unless set. Partly closed: Databricks proving runs now use a service principal (OAuth machine to machine), not a stored user token. The examples repo was not re-audited.
  7. Reliability (hardening experiments E-01 to E-05, tasks/hardening/): append is not rerun-safe (F-011, F-019), killed runs stay running (F-013), pandas lacks overwrite_partitions and REST (F-012, F-015), hashing costs about 4 s per million rows on pandas (F-014). Closed: append reruns and killed runs by ADR 008 and its follow-ups (F-011, F-013, F-019, F-031); pandas overwrite_partitions (F-012) and REST on pandas (F-015); hashing made faster (F-014, about 1.5 s per million rows on pandas after the fix).

docs.title: Tutorial 1: prove one workload gives the same result on pandas and Spark
docs.text: You will run one task twice, on the pandas backend and on local Spark, and have Ubunye compare the two run records. It is for anyone who wants to see, on their own machine, that "runs the same everywhere" is checked and not just claimed. About ten minutes; no cloud, no account.

docs.title: You need
docs.text:
• Python and, for the Spark half, Java, in the versions listed in Installation. The pandas half needs no Java.
  • The Ubunye repository (the workload lives in it):
git clone https://github.com/ubunye-ai-ecosystems/ubunye_engine
cd ubunye_engine/examples/proving/c01_portable_etl
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate            # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install "ubunye-engine[pandas,spark]"

docs.title: 1. Run it on pandas
docs.text:
ubunye run -d pipelines -u proving -p c01 -t etl --backend pandas --lineage --var out_dir=output/pandas
ubunye prove observe --workload c01-portable-etl --env pandas-local \
  -d pipelines -u proving -p c01 -t etl -o evidence

--lineage keeps a run record: for each input and output, every row's hash, the schema and the row count. prove observe files that record as evidence of this workload in this environment.

The run prints a UserWarning from Narwhals, Found complex group-by expression, which can't be expressed efficiently with the pandas API. That is expected: it is about speed on pandas, not about the result. The run still ends with [OK] Run complete for etl.

docs.title: 2. Run the same task on Spark
docs.text:
ubunye run -d pipelines -u proving -p c01 -t etl --backend spark --lineage --var out_dir=output/spark
ubunye prove observe --workload c01-portable-etl --env spark-local \
  -d pipelines -u proving -p c01 -t etl -o evidence

Nothing in the task changed: not the config, not transformations.py.

docs.title: 3. Compare
docs.text:
ubunye prove report evidence --workload c01-portable-etl --reference spark-local

Expected:

| Environment | Verdict | Execute | Identity | Inputs | Data | Schema | Rows | Digest | ...
| spark-local | **PASS** | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | bb08a7d7a9fd | ...
| pandas-local | **PASS** | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | bb08a7d7a9fd | ...

Each row is one run. spark-local is the reference: the run every other run is compared with. The columns, in plain words:

Column PASS means Verdict every check below passed Execute the run finished without an error Identity it is the same job: the same code, the same output names, and the same time zone for cutting time into days Inputs it read the same rows Data it wrote the same rows Schema the outputs have the same columns and types Rows the outputs have the same number of rows Digest a short fingerprint of all the output rows; equal digests mean equal data Time, Cost, Engine how long the task took, where the cost figure came from, and the Ubunye version and backend

The command exits with 0 when no run disagrees, and with 1 when one does.

Data PASS means both engines wrote the same rows: every value, every null, every type, compared by a hash of every row that ignores row and column order and reads timestamps as UTC instants. It does not mean the Parquet files are byte for byte the same; they are not, and Ubunye does not claim they are.

The digest bb08a7d7a9fd was first measured on Windows (Spark 4.2, pandas 3) and is pinned in the repository's integration test, which CI runs on Linux with Spark 3.5 and Spark 4: yours should match. If it does not, that is worth a report.

docs.title: When it disagrees
docs.text:
Try it: make the Spark run cut time into days in another time zone. Open pipelines/proving/c01/etl/config.yaml and add this block at the end of the file, at the top level (not indented, next to MODEL, VERSION and CONFIG):

ENGINE:
  spark_conf:
    spark.sql.session.timeZone: Africa/Johannesburg

Then rerun only the Spark half (both commands of step 2), then the report. Expected:

| spark-local | **PASS** | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | 09f629ed5b5f | ...
| pandas-local | **FAIL** | PASS | FAIL | PASS | FAIL | PASS | PASS | bb08a7d7a9fd | ...

Why:

- **pandas-local**: session time zone UTC, reference Africa/Johannesburg: day and hour values can differ

The pandas-local row now says FAIL, with Identity and Data FAIL, and Why: gives the reason: the two runs cut time into days in different time zones. The report exits with 1, so a script or a CI job stops here.

This is the first problem the proving ground found: a Spark session on a laptop outside UTC used to cut days in the laptop's own time zone, without saying so. Ubunye now runs every session in UTC unless you set a time zone, as you just did. Why it works this way: ADR 007.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
Remove the ENGINE: block you added to pipelines/proving/c01/etl/config.yaml, so the task is back as it was (or run git checkout pipelines/proving/c01/etl/config.yaml). Then delete what the runs wrote:

rm -rf output evidence pipelines/.ubunye

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
• JAVA_HOME is not set: install Java (versions in Installation) and point JAVA_HOME at it, or do only the pandas half.
  • Windows: Spark needs HADOOP_HOME with winutils.exe to write files.
  • pyarrow older than 24 on Windows cannot find a time zone database; upgrade it.

docs.title: Tutorial 2: nine messy tables to a fact table, with checks that catch the mess
docs.text:
You will build what a data team builds first on an online shop's data: one row per order, then monthly numbers per seller. The data is shaped like the Olist Brazilian e-commerce set: nine CSV files, each with its own problems. On the way you will see four Ubunye features stop four kinds of bad data, and then break the pipeline on purpose to watch them work.

This tutorial teaches data checks: quarantine (set bad rows aside with a label), reconcile (prove no rows or money went missing) and input contracts (stop a run when a source file changes shape). The reference for every check is Expectations.

About 20 minutes. No cloud, no account, no Java (Spark is an optional last step).

docs.title: You need
docs.text:
• Python, in a version listed in Installation.
  • The Ubunye repository (the example lives in it):
git clone https://github.com/ubunye-ai-ecosystems/ubunye_engine
cd ubunye_engine/examples/real-world/olist_ecommerce
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate            # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install "ubunye-engine[pandas]" "narwhals>=2.9"

This needs Ubunye 0.8.0 or newer. Older versions have no columns input contracts and miss fixes this example led to (clean reasons on quarantined rows, the error kept in a failed run's record, a short message instead of a traceback when a check stops a run), so they fail at step 2. To run against the repository you just cloned instead, use pip install -e "../../..[pandas]" "narwhals>=2.9" (../../.. is its top folder).

Every command below runs from this folder.

docs.title: 1. Look at the data
docs.text:
ls sample

Nine files: orders, order items, payments, reviews, customers, sellers, products, geolocation (points per zip code) and a table that translates category names from Portuguese to English. They are a small made up sample (60 orders) with the same file names, columns and formats as the real Olist files, so the same pipeline reads both.

The pipeline has three steps, each a folder under pipelines/olist/sales/ with a config.yaml (what to read, write and check) and a transformations.py (the logic):

Step Reads Writes clean the nine raw files typed tables, and the bad rows set aside orders_fact what clean wrote one row per order monthly what the first two wrote sales per seller and month, and per category and month

docs.title: 2. Clean the raw files
docs.text:
ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t clean --backend pandas --lineage

Expected: [OK] Run complete for clean. A lot was checked on the way. See what was set aside:

python -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.read_parquet('output/order_items_rejected')[['order_id', 'price', '_ubunye_failed_rules']])"
python -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.read_parquet('output/payments_rejected')[['payment_type', 'payment_value', '_ubunye_failed_rules']])"
python -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.read_parquet('output/reviews_rejected')[['review_score', '_ubunye_failed_rules']])"

Three bad rows, one of each kind: an item priced 0.00, a payment of type pix that the rules do not know, a review scored 7 (scores go from 1 to 5). Each carries the rule it broke. This is quarantine: the bad rows are kept and labelled, not dropped and not mixed in with the good ones. In pipelines/olist/sales/clean/config.yaml:

    order_items:
      quarantine: order_items_rejected   # where bad rows go
      max_quarantine_rate: 0.05          # more than 5% bad: stop, the source has changed
      rules:
        - between: {column: price, min: 0.01}
          severity: quarantine

Two more features ran before any of this. Input contracts checked each raw file's columns and types right after it was read, before the transform ran:

    raw_orders:
      rules:
        - columns:
            order_id: string
            order_purchase_timestamp: timestamp
            ...

And a reconcile checked that no row went missing between the raw file and the output. Set aside counts as arrived: it has a reason, it is not lost.

docs.title: 3. Read the run record
docs.text:
--lineage kept a record of the run: every input and output, how many rows, a hash of every row, and every check with its result.

ubunye lineage trace -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t clean

At the end, under EXPECTATIONS, every check is listed. For example:

    quarantine order_items.price_between                1/80
    ok         order_items.freight_value_between        0/80
    ok         order_items.rows_from_raw_items          0/80
               80 rows read from raw_items, 80 reached order_items: 0 lost, 0 gained (at most 0 lost, at most 0 gained)

docs.title: 4. Build the fact table and the monthly numbers
docs.text:
ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t orders_fact --backend pandas --lineage
ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t monthly     --backend pandas --lineage

orders_fact warns, and goes on:

expectation warning: orders_fact: payment_gap_between (between) broken by 4 of 60 rows

Four orders were paid more or less than their items and freight, by over one real. Look at them:

python -c "import pandas as pd; f = pd.read_parquet('output/orders_fact'); print(f[f.payment_gap.abs() > 1][['order_status', 'items_price', 'freight', 'payments_total', 'payment_gap']])"

Each has a reason: a canceled order that was paid; instalment interest (paid 3.20 more); an order whose free item was set aside in step 2, so its freight is missing; and the order whose pix payment was set aside, so it looks unpaid. A warning is for things worth knowing but not worth stopping for. The count is in the run record.

One order is not in the table at all:

python -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.read_parquet('output/orders_fact_rejected')[['order_id', 'delivery_days', '_ubunye_failed_rules']])"

It was delivered 3 days before it was bought: the dates are wrong, so it waits here for someone to fix them. And the reconcile on the fact table still passed:

ubunye lineage trace -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t orders_fact

    ok         orders_fact.rows_from_orders             0/60
               60 rows read from orders, 60 reached orders_fact: 0 lost, 0 gained (at most 0 lost, at most 0 gained)
    ok         orders_fact.payments_total_sum_from_payments 0/1
               sum of payment_value in payments 7411.88, of payments_total in orders_fact 7411.88: difference 0 (at most 0.01)

Every order arrived once (59 in the table, 1 set aside), and every real paid is in the table. (The item price sum shows a difference like 1.8e-12: that is how floating point numbers add up, and why the config allows 0.01.)

Finally, the monthly table:

python -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.read_parquet('output/seller_monthly').sort_values(['seller_id', 'purchase_month']))"

docs.title: 5. Break it: a source file changes
docs.text:
A colleague opens the orders file in a spreadsheet and saves it; one purchase time comes back as 18/02/2018 10:59. Make that copy in data/ (git ignores that folder):

python -c "import shutil, pathlib; shutil.copytree('sample', 'data', dirs_exist_ok=True); p = pathlib.Path('data/olist_orders_dataset.csv'); p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('2018-02-18 10:59:08', '18/02/2018 10:59', 1))"
ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t clean --backend pandas --var data_dir=data --var out_dir=output-bad

Expected:

Starting task: clean (Mode: DEV, Deploy: client)
[ERROR] Run stopped for clean: An input broke its expectations, so the transform did not run and nothing was written:
  raw_orders: columns (columns): order_purchase_timestamp: expected timestamp, found string
  Hint: The source has changed. Fix it, or change the input's expectations in CONFIG.expectations if the change is meant.

One bad value turned the whole column into text. Without the contract, the pipeline would have run on, and every date calculation on that column would have failed later, or worse, given wrong numbers. The contract stopped it at the door, named the column, and wrote nothing: output-bad does not exist.

docs.title: 6. Break it: a join loses orders
docs.text:
The most common silent bug in a fact table: an inner join where a left join was needed. Open pipelines/olist/sales/orders_fact/transformations.py and change only this one line, the join with per_order_items (the file has other joins; a find and replace of every how="left" would break those too and give a different error):

            .join(per_order_items, on="order_id", how="left")

to

            .join(per_order_items, on="order_id", how="inner")

Save, and run the step again:

ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t orders_fact --backend pandas --lineage

Expected:

Starting task: orders_fact (Mode: DEV, Deploy: client)
expectation warning: orders_fact: payment_gap_between (between) broken by 3 of 59 rows
[ERROR] Run stopped for orders_fact: Expectations failed, so nothing was written:
  orders_fact: rows_from_orders (reconcile): 60 rows read from orders, 59 reached orders_fact: 1 lost, 0 gained (at most 0 lost, at most 0 gained)
  orders_fact: payments_total_sum_from_payments (reconcile): sum of payment_value in payments 7411.88, of payments_total in orders_fact 7365.98: difference -45.900000000000546 (at most 0.01)
  Hint: A reconcile: look for a join or filter that loses rows, or a source that changed; if the loss is expected, allow a share (max_lost: "1%") or set severity: warn. A reconcile cannot quarantine.

The canceled order has no items, so the inner join dropped it, and its 45.90 payment with it. (The warning now counts 3 of 59 rows: the lost order was one of the four.) Both reconciles saw it; the run wrote nothing, so yesterday's good table is still there. The run record keeps why:

ubunye lineage trace -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t orders_fact

Run:     ...  [error]  ...
Error:   ExpectationError: Expectations failed, so nothing was written: ...

Change inner back to left before going on.

docs.title: 7. Optional: the same answer on Spark
docs.text:
Every step is written once with Narwhals, so it runs on Spark unchanged. With Java installed (versions in Installation; Windows also needs HADOOP_HOME with winutils.exe):

pip install "ubunye-engine[pandas,spark]"
for t in clean orders_fact monthly; do
  ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t --backend pandas --lineage --var out_dir=output/pandas
  ubunye prove observe --workload r2-olist-$t --env pandas-local -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t -o evidence
done
for t in clean orders_fact monthly; do
  ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t --backend spark --lineage --var out_dir=output/spark
  ubunye prove observe --workload r2-olist-$t --env spark-local -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t -o evidence
done
ubunye prove report evidence --workload r2-olist-orders_fact --reference spark-local

In PowerShell (Windows), the loops are written like this:

pip install "ubunye-engine[pandas,spark]"
foreach ($t in "clean", "orders_fact", "monthly") {
  ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t --backend pandas --lineage --var out_dir=output/pandas
  ubunye prove observe --workload "r2-olist-$t" --env pandas-local -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t -o evidence
}
foreach ($t in "clean", "orders_fact", "monthly") {
  ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t --backend spark --lineage --var out_dir=output/spark
  ubunye prove observe --workload "r2-olist-$t" --env spark-local -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t -o evidence
}
ubunye prove report evidence --workload r2-olist-orders_fact --reference spark-local

(After the runs, one ubunye prove observe --workload r2-olist ... -t clean -t orders_fact -t monthly does the same three observations, named the same way.) Every dimension should say PASS, with the same digest on both engines: 6affe2f5382c for clean, 6dcf270328d8 for orders_fact, a0bd206029ca for monthly. The repository's tests check these digests on pandas, and on Spark 3.5 and 4 in CI.

docs.title: 8. The real data
docs.text:
The real Olist data (about 100,000 orders) is on Kaggle under a non-commercial licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), so it is not in the repository. Download it when you run:

pip install kaggle        # plus a Kaggle API token: https://www.kaggle.com/settings
kaggle datasets download -d olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce -p data --unzip
for t in clean orders_fact monthly; do
  ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t --backend pandas --lineage --var data_dir=data --var out_dir=output-real
done

The kaggle line works in any shell (scripts/fetch_data.sh does the same in bash). In PowerShell, the loop is:

foreach ($t in "clean", "orders_fact", "monthly") {
  ubunye run -d pipelines -u olist -p sales -t $t --backend pandas --lineage --var data_dir=data --var out_dir=output-real
}

Nothing in the pipeline changes: only where the data is. On the full data (99,441 orders), measured once on one Windows machine with pandas: clean 16 s, orders_fact 31 s, monthly 3 s. All 99,441 orders reached the fact table, both money reconciles passed, and 1,022 orders were paid more or less than their items and freight by over one real (the warning).

docs.title: What each feature caught
docs.text: Feature Where What it caught in this tutorial Input contract clean one date saved the wrong way turned a column to text (step 5) Quarantine clean, orders_fact a free item, an unknown payment type, a score of 7, an order delivered before it was bought Reconcile clean, orders_fact an inner join that lost a canceled order and its 45.90 (step 6) Warning orders_fact four orders paid more or less than they cost Run record every step every check, every count, and why a run failed

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
rm -rf output output-bad output-real data evidence pipelines/.ubunye

In PowerShell:

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force output, output-bad, output-real, data, evidence, pipelines/.ubunye -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
• ImportError: the example needs narwhals>=2.9 (Expr.floor): upgrade Narwhals (pip install -U narwhals). Every step checks this first.
  • pyarrow older than 24 on Windows cannot find a time zone database; upgrade it.
  • kaggle: command not found or 401: install the kaggle package and put your API token where https://github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-api says (kaggle.json).
